articles.title: Stephen A. Smith faces backlash for mocking Lane Johnson's mental health reasons for retiring
articles.summary: Stephen A.
articles.body: Stephen A. Smith has found himself at the center of a heated controversy after his comments about Lane Johnson’s decision to retire from the NFL sparked backlash from viewers and even an uncomfortable moment among his fellow First Take panelists. Johnson, the longtime Philadelphia Eagles offensive tackle, announced his retirement Tuesday after 14 NFL seasons. The 36-year-old said he had reached the difficult decision after reflecting on his personal and family priorities and realizing that he needed to focus on his mental health.Fans slam Stephen A. Smith over Lane Johnson mental health comments during heated First Take segmentOn Wednesday’s episode of ESPN’s First Take, Smith discussed the impact Johnson’s retirement could have on an Eagles team already dealing with a number of injuries and struggles.But his commentary quickly shifted toward questioning the timing of Johnson’s decision and his stated reason for stepping away. Smith repeatedly emphasized that Johnson did not retire during the offseason but instead walked away four games into the season. He then sarcastically repeated Johnson’s decision to prioritize his mental health, prompting an increasingly uncomfortable atmosphere at the desk.Smith questioned why Johnson would leave while Philadelphia was dealing with a difficult stretch, particularly given how important the veteran offensive tackle was to the Eagles. At one point, Smith mockingly repeated the phrase “my mental health,” before arguing that the situation surrounding the Eagles had become so chaotic that it could push someone toward walking away from football.The viewers accused Smith of making light of Johnson’s mental health struggles rather than simply criticizing the timing of his retirement.Kimberley A. Martin calls Stephen A. Smith outThe moment became even more uncomfortable when Kimberley A. Martin appeared to challenge Smith over his tone. After Smith finished his rant, Martin told him that she felt he was “making light of the situation.”Smith immediately pushed back, appearing surprised by the criticism. Martin clarified that she was referring to the suggestion that playing for the Eagles was somehow what caused Johnson to reach the point of stepping away. Her intervention changed the tone of the discussion, forcing Smith to explain what he meant.Stephen A. Smith attempts to clarify his commentsSmith subsequently insisted that he was not making fun of mental health.“Let me be very, very clear,” Smith said, explaining that he would never make light of mental health issues.Instead, Smith argued that his criticism was directed at the Eagles and the chaotic circumstances surrounding the team. He pointed to Johnson’s importance to Philadelphia’s offensive line and argued that it was significant that an elite player would choose to walk away in the middle of a season.Smith maintained that his larger point was that the Eagles’ situation had become so stressful that it could contribute to someone deciding that continuing to play was no longer worth it. Still, the clarification came after viewers had already reacted strongly to the original segment.Johnson’s history made the discussion particularly sensitive. The veteran tackle has previously spoken publicly about dealing with anxiety and depression, and he stepped away from the Eagles during the 2021 season while addressing his mental health.He also indicated before the 2026 season that retirement had already been something he had considered. During training camp, Johnson discussed how his priorities had changed as his children grew older and his parents aged.His retirement statement ultimately framed the decision around his family, personal priorities and mental health rather than a single incident with the Eagles.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: What happened to Sam Beal: The Former Giants CB who told his girlfriend he was coming home, nearly 15 months later, he’s still missing
articles.summary: Former New York Giants cornerback Sam Beal has now been missing for nearly 15 months, with his family still searching for answers after his disappearance
articles.body: Former New York Giants cornerback Sam Beal has now been missing for nearly 15 months, with his family still searching for answers after his disappearance took him from Michigan to Virginia Beach under circumstances that remain unexplained.Beal, who was selected by the Giants in the third round of the 2018 NFL Supplemental Draft, was last seen in July 2025. According to the missing-person information made public through the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System (NamUs), Beal was last seen by his girlfriend on July 12, 2025, after dropping her off at a family member’s home in the Caledonia, Michigan, area. He was supposed to head to work afterward.Instead, according to the report, Beal borrowed his girlfriend’s vehicle and traveled toward Virginia Beach, Virginia, a destination that has become central to the mystery surrounding his disappearance.More than a year later, his whereabouts remain unknown.Sam Beal’s last known movements remain at the center of the caseThe timeline surrounding Beal’s disappearance is particularly puzzling. According to the missing-person report, Beal dropped his girlfriend off on July 12 and borrowed her vehicle because he was expected to go to work. He did not make it to work.At some point, Beal traveled roughly 750 miles from Michigan to Virginia Beach. The following day, July 13, he spoke with his girlfriend by phone. Beal reportedly told her that he was in Virginia Beach and planned to head back home.That would be the last known communication from him. According to the publicly available missing-person information, Beal never returned home and has not been seen or heard from since that phone call.The National Missing and Unidentified Persons System lists the circumstances of his disappearance as unknown. The Black and Missing Foundation's current listing also identifies July 12, 2025, as his missing date and says there has been no known contact since the July 13 phone call.His girlfriend’s car was later found in Virginia BeachOne of the most striking details in the case involves the vehicle Beal had borrowed. The car was eventually recovered in Virginia Beach by a member of his girlfriend’s family. But Beal was not inside. According to the missing-person report, his shoes and socks were found on the floor of the front passenger area of the vehicle. Investigators also noted sand on the floor.The detail has naturally become one of the central pieces of information surrounding the disappearance, but it is important not to assign a meaning to it that investigators have not publicly established.There is no verified public evidence showing exactly why Beal’s shoes and socks were inside the vehicle, where he went after leaving the car, or what happened to him afterward. The available case information simply lists his circumstances of disappearance as unknown.Beal apparently left with very littleThe missing-person report also provides an important detail about what Beal had with him. According to the report, he did not appear to leave Michigan with luggage or a substantial collection of personal belongings. He reportedly had the clothes he was wearing, a pair of slides and a wallet containing his driver's license and banking card.That makes the disappearance even more difficult for his family to understand. There has been no confirmed public sighting of Beal after the July 13 phone call, and authorities have not publicly established where he went after the vehicle was recovered.The investigation involves Michigan and Virginia Beach authoritiesThe case began in Michigan but quickly developed a Virginia connection because that is where Beal and the vehicle were last known to be.According to reporting from WTVR, Beal’s family initially contacted the Virginia Beach Police Department but was directed to the Kentwood Police Department in Michigan, which became the department of record for the investigation. Virginia Beach police have said they are assisting Kentwood police.A significant timeline detail emerged in January 2026. The family said a police report had been filed with Kentwood police in August 2025, while Beal was not entered into the national missing-person database until October.By January 2026, the case had received renewed public attention after Beal’s sister, Essence Zhane, publicly pleaded for help. At that point, the family had gone approximately seven months without hearing from him.His sister has repeatedly asked the public for helpBeal’s sister has been one of the most visible voices keeping attention on the disappearance. In January, Essence Zhane said the family had spent months trying to piece together what happened and was desperate for answers. She emphasized that she was not looking for speculation about the disappearance but wanted information that could help the family understand what happened to her brother.Her public appeals have continued. In June 2026, nearly a year after Beal disappeared, his sister again shared information about the case, according to reporting by the New York Post. At that point, there had still been no public breakthrough in the investigation. That means that, as of October 2026, Beal's family has now been living with the uncertainty for nearly 15 months.What happened to Sam Beal after Virginia Beach?That remains the biggest unanswered question. The publicly available information establishes that Beal traveled from Michigan to Virginia Beach, spoke with his girlfriend on July 13 and said he intended to return home.He never did.His girlfriend’s vehicle was later recovered in Virginia Beach with his shoes and socks inside, along with sand on the floor. Beyond those facts, there is a significant gap in the public timeline.There has been no confirmed public sighting, verified communication or publicly announced resolution explaining where Beal went after that final phone conversation.It is also important not to treat online theories about his disappearance as established facts. The available official and law-enforcement-derived information does not publicly establish what happened to Beal or why he traveled to Virginia Beach.Some additional information about Beal's life before his disappearance emerged in January 2026 after the New York Post obtained a Kentwood police report through a Freedom of Information Act request. The report contained accounts from people who said Beal had experienced difficulties after his NFL career ended, as well as other personal circumstances in the period before his disappearance.Those details should be treated carefully. They provide context about Beal's life before July 2025, but they do not establish what happened to him, and they should not be presented as an explanation for his disappearance. The investigation remains unresolved publicly.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes' $504.75 million contract still leaves him nearly $490 million behind Tom Brady's $650 million fortune
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes signed an eight-year, $504.75 million deal with the Kansas City Chiefs in June 2026, yet his estimated net worth sits at $160 million.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes signed an eight-year, $504.75 million deal with the Kansas City Chiefs in June 2026, yet his estimated net worth sits at $160 million. Tom Brady, retired since 2023, is valued at $650 million. That leaves a gap of roughly $490 million, close to half a billion dollars. Those are Celebrity Net Worth estimates, not audited accounts. Timing, ownership stakes and a Fox Sports contract explain most of the difference. Brady built his fortune over 23 seasons and a second career in broadcasting. Mahomes is only in his 10th season.How does Mahomes' $504.75 million contract compare with Tom Brady's $650 million fortune?A contract is not a bank balance, and that is where most of the confusion starts. Mahomes' $504.75 million is spread across eight seasons, 2026 through 2033. He collects $56.75 million in cash this year, rising to $70 million in the final season. Only $150 million was fully guaranteed at signing. Incentives could lift the total to $522.25 million, but none of that arrives in one payment.Put the contract next to Brady's $650 million and the gap is about $145 million, not half a billion. The big number appears when you compare net worths instead. Mahomes sits at $160 million. Brady sits at $650 million. The spread is $490 million.So why does a $504.75 million deal translate to a $160 million fortune? Because most of it has not been paid. Celebrity Net Worth tracks about $289 million in career cash for Mahomes through this season. Taxes, fees and spending come out of that, so a net worth well below career earnings is normal.What did Tom Brady actually earn in 23 NFL seasons?About $333 million in salary. That number surprises people. Brady made roughly $230 million of it across 20 years in New England, often by restructuring deals so the Patriots had cap room. He earned around $28.3 million in 2020, $39.4 million in 2021 and about $30 million in 2022 with Tampa Bay. Endorsements added well over $100 million. Salary and sponsors together passed $450 million before taxes.Here is the twist. Mahomes is on pace to pass Brady's entire career salary by the end of next season. Celebrity Net Worth's projections put his cumulative cash at $346.75 million after 2027, which clears Brady's $333 million. Brady needed 23 years. Mahomes needs 11, and he will do it while still in his early thirties.Why did retirement make Tom Brady richer than his playing days?Because the largest gains came after the last snap. Fox signed Brady in 2022 to a 10-year, $375 million contract, an average of $37.5 million a year. He skipped the 2023 season, debuted in the booth in September 2024 and is back for a third year. If the money is paid evenly, his first two seasons are worth roughly $75 million. That deal alone could out-earn his 23 years of playing salary.The bigger driver is the Raiders. NFL owners approved Brady's 5% stake in October 2024. He and partner Tom Wagner paid $220 million for a combined 10%, so Brady's share cost about $110 million before fees, or roughly $122 million with his half of an extra $24 million in fees. In May 2026, a deal for more than 25% of the team valued the Raiders at about $9.9 billion. At a round $10 billion, Brady's slice is worth around $500 million on paper.That single asset is worth more than three times Mahomes' entire net worth. It comes with caveats. The stake is private, non-controlling and hard to sell, so $500 million is a benchmark, not a payout. Not every bet worked, either. His FTX shares were wiped out when the exchange collapsed in November 2022.Brady also has a say in how the team is run. He has described his role as strategic advisory and works with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick in the 2026 draft. Owning a team while calling games for Fox also limits his access to opposing teams.## What does Mahomes own away from the field?Quite a lot. He holds minority stakes in the Kansas City Royals, bought in August 2020, and in Sporting Kansas City. His wife, Brittany, was a founding investor in the NWSL's Kansas City Current, and Patrick later joined that ownership group. In 2023 he and Travis Kelce joined investors who bought into the Alpine Formula 1 team.The catch is that none of the purchase prices or stake sizes were disclosed. That leaves estimators guessing, so his $160 million is harder to pin down than Brady's Raiders figure, which has real numbers behind it. Add endorsements from Adidas, State Farm, Oakley, T-Mobile, Hy-Vee and others, and his off-field income is already substantial.Can Patrick Mahomes ever catch Tom Brady's fortune?The contract runs through 2033, when Mahomes will be 38. If he collects all of his scheduled base pay, career cash would approach $737 million before endorsements. Kansas City reworked the deal in 2023, restructured it again early in 2026 and rewrote it in June, and Celebrity Net Worth expects another revisit before it expires.Health is the variable nobody can price. Mahomes tore his ACL and LCL in December 2025, in a season that ended with Kansas City at 6-11 and out of the playoffs for the first time in his career as a starter. He was cleared for training camp in July and said in August the knee felt strong.The real lesson from Brady's climb is that equity has done more than salary. One of his most valuable assets is a Raiders stake that cost about $110 million. Mahomes will collect $56.75 million this year and a scheduled $58 million in 2027, which adds up to $114.75 million in cash. That is already more than Brady paid for the stake that now anchors his fortune.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce’s mom Donna Kelce helped raise $4,100 for students’ lunch debt with her famous cookie recipe
articles.summary: In 2024, Donna Kelce’s famous family cookie recipe became more than a beloved treat.
articles.body: In 2024, Donna Kelce’s famous family cookie recipe became more than a beloved treat. It turned into a small but meaningful fundraising effort for Kansas schoolchildren struggling with lunch debt. A local business owner received permission from the mother of NFL stars Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce to place the recipe on handmade mugs, with part of every sale going towards school meal debt. What began with a simple idea had already raised $4,100 by February 2024, giving the project a bigger impact than its modest beginnings suggested.Donna Kelce’s cookie recipe helped raise $4,100The idea came from Annie Stowe, owner of Annie’s Barn, a small business where she makes mugs in the basement of her Overland Park home. Stowe first crossed paths with Donna after Kelce purchased 20 mugs as Christmas gifts in 2023.After the purchase, Stowe contacted Donna with a charitable proposal. She wanted to feature the famous chocolate chip cookie recipe Donna had made for Travis and Jason on a new mug. Donna agreed, allowing Stowe to donate $5 from every mug sold to help clear lunch debt at local elementary schools.The mugs were priced at $18 and featured the recipe alongside an iPhone Memoji-style image of Donna. The personal touch helped turn a piece of Kelce family history into a fundraiser with a practical goal.Stowe initially revealed that the sales had generated $2,000 in 2023. After a local television report highlighted the effort, another $2,100 came in, taking the total to $4,100.“We sold enough mugs to raise $2,000 [in 2023],” Stowe told PEOPLE.The money went through Stowe’s Out of the Red Friday initiative, which focuses on paying off school lunch debt.Donna Kelce’s charity effort gives her cookie recipe a new purposeThe fundraiser came at a time when school meal debt remained a serious issue for families across the United States. Stowe’s project offered a direct way for customers to contribute while buying a handmade item tied to one of football’s best-known families.The campaign also reflected Donna’s willingness to share something personal for a cause involving children. Her cookie recipe had already become part of the Kelce family's public story after she became widely recognised for making the treats for Travis and Jason.Donna previously described the recipe as something especially meaningful to her.“I’m like, ‘What has my life become?’”She also explained why she hoped others would make the cookies themselves:“It’s an absolute favorite for me and everyone in the family” and that she hopes other people “will enjoy them as much as we have through the years and gather in the kitchen with their own families and friends to bake them, just as I do with mine.”For Stowe, the next step was potentially delivering the funds directly to schools with Donna. She said she had invited Kelce to join her, although the Super Bowl schedule made the timing difficult.The fundraiser showed how a simple family recipe could take on a second life. In this case, every mug sold helped turn Donna Kelce’s famous cookies into support for children who needed help with school meals.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "His soul appeared broken": Tom Brady reportedly risked his NFL season in desperate attempt to save marriage with Gisele Bündchen
articles.summary: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen's divorce may have looked sudden to the public, but a new report paints a different picture of what happened behind closed
articles.body: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen's divorce may have looked sudden to the public, but a new report paints a different picture of what happened behind closed doors. The former NFL quarterback reportedly took an unusual break from Tampa Bay Buccaneers training camp in 2022 as he tried to repair his troubled marriage. According to a book cited by The Comeback, Brady's decision to continue playing football had become a major source of tension between the couple. His reported 11-day absence came during an increasingly difficult period that eventually ended their 13-year marriage.Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen faced growing marriage tensionBrady and Bündchen began dating in 2006 and married in 2009. Together, they became one of the world's most recognisable celebrity couples, raising two children while balancing Brady's NFL career and Bündchen's modelling success.Their relationship reportedly began to fracture years before their divorce. The biggest disagreement centred on Brady's football future.Brady announced his retirement after the 2021 season, but reversed the decision months later and returned for the 2022 campaign. According to the report, Bündchen struggled with the choice and eventually travelled to Costa Rica.The Comeback cited author Las Anderson's book, which reportedly details how seriously the situation affected Brady during training camp.Former Buccaneers coach Bruce Arians described the change in Brady's appearance at the time.“For someone with Tom's build to lose that much weight was a huge change,”Another coach offered an even more striking description of Brady's condition:“It looked like cheekbones were popping out above his cheekbones. It may sound rude, but he looked like a cancer patient with only great hair,”The comments were presented in the report as observations of Brady's appearance during a period of intense personal pressure.Tom Brady reportedly took 11-day leave to save marriageThe most dramatic detail concerns Brady's decision to step away from the Buccaneers during training camp. According to Anderson's book, he requested an extended leave and travelled to a private resort in the Bahamas in what was described as an attempt to resolve the crisis with Bündchen.“At the end of August, Brady requested a long-term camp leave from his coach for the first time in his career. He said he would return, but did not say when. The situation had deteriorated so much that he and Gisele had to have a serious conversation in a secluded place,”The report says Brady eventually returned to Tampa Bay after 11 days. However, the effort did not repair the relationship.“When he returned to Tampa Bay after an 11-day leave, his soul appeared even more broken than before,”Brady and Bündchen finalized their divorce in October 2022. Their split ended a marriage that had attracted enormous public attention for more than a decade.Bündchen later moved forward with her life and welcomed her third child with Brazilian jiu-jitsu instructor Joaquim Valente in February 2025. Brady, meanwhile, continued building his career away from the NFL after retiring from professional football.The latest account adds another layer to one of the most closely followed celebrity breakups in sports, suggesting that Brady made a serious attempt to preserve his family before the marriage ultimately came to an end.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Josh Allen’s $75K donation boosts children’s care as his impact on Buffalo goes far beyond football
articles.summary: Earlier this year, Josh Allen’s influence in Buffalo reached well beyond the football field when a community fundraising effort connected to the Bills
articles.body: Earlier this year, Josh Allen’s influence in Buffalo reached well beyond the football field when a community fundraising effort connected to the Bills quarterback helped deliver $75,000 to Golisano Children’s Hospital of Buffalo. The contribution supports the Patricia Allen Fund, named after Allen’s late grandmother, and will help strengthen care for young patients. The donation also reflects the unusual connection Allen has built with Buffalo, where his name has become tied not only to football success but also to local causes. With the Bills, Wegmans and passionate fans all playing a role, a product inspired by Allen turned into something with a far greater purpose.Josh Allen’s Buffalo connection helps support children’s hospital careThe $75,000 contribution was presented at Golisano Children’s Hospital, bringing together hospital leaders, Buffalo Bills representatives and Wegmans. The Patricia Allen Fund helps provide resources for areas where children and their families may need urgent support, including the emergency department and pediatric intensive care unit.Hospital president Dr. Stephen Turkovich also highlighted the wider role the Bills play in the community.“They are not just a football team, they are really a tremendous community asset,” he said.That sentiment captures why Allen’s charitable work has resonated in Buffalo. His connection with the city has grown steadily throughout his career, and the fund carrying his grandmother’s name has given that relationship an even more personal meaning.The timing also came as Allen entered a new chapter away from football. He and Hailee Steinfeld recently welcomed their daughter, prompting Turkovich to offer a warm message to the Bills star.“Welcome to fatherhood… we’re very excited to welcome you into that club,” he said.Wegmans and Bills fans turn Josh Allen cereal into charityThe donation grew from an unexpected source: sales of Wegmans’ Josh Allen MVP Puffs cereal. What could have been just another athlete-branded product became a way for Buffalo fans to contribute to children receiving medical care.Wegmans community relations manager Michele Mehaffy said the response from shoppers helped transform the campaign into something much bigger.The initiative showed how Allen’s popularity can create an impact even when he is not on the field. Each purchase helped build momentum for the Patricia Allen Fund and its work supporting children and families during difficult moments.Mehaffy also pointed to the quarterback’s strong bond with the city.“We know the love that our quarterback has for this place,” she said.For Allen, the $75,000 donation adds another chapter to a growing legacy in Buffalo. His football achievements remain central to his identity, but efforts like this show why his influence in the region extends far beyond Sundays.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Cheated on repeatedly": Sarah Jane Ramos makes major career move after turbulent split from Dak Prescott
articles.summary: Sarah Jane Ramos is turning the page after her highly publicized split from Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott, with her latest moves pointing toward
articles.body: Sarah Jane Ramos is turning the page after her highly publicized split from Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott, with her latest moves pointing toward a future built around her own career. Ramos has shown interest in real estate, taken on a new public role in Dallas and continued developing her professional identity. Her latest steps come months after the couple called off their planned wedding in Italy, ending a relationship that had included two daughters and a highly publicized engagement.Sarah Jane Ramos explores real estate after Dak Prescott splitRamos recently gave followers a glimpse of her latest goal by sharing a photo of a Law of Agency textbook. The material is linked to a 30-hour course through Champions School of Real Estate, suggesting she is working toward expanding her professional options.Her Instagram update indicated that she had completed two-sixths of the course. While she has not publicly detailed her long-term plans in real estate, the move gives her career another direction beyond her previous work in the wine and spirits industry.Ramos is also stepping into a more prominent role in Dallas. She was announced as the host of The Huddle Table, a dinner organised by the National Football Wives Association. The opportunity puts her in a setting where she can build professional connections and strengthen a public profile separate from her former relationship.Dak Prescott and Sarah Jane Ramos’ relationship ended before weddingRamos and Prescott began dating in 2023 and later became parents to two daughters, Margaret Jane Rose and Aurora Rayne. Prescott proposed in October 2024, with the couple planning to marry in Lake Como, Italy, in April 2026.That wedding never happened. The couple called off their plans in March, just weeks before the scheduled ceremony. At the time, Ramos’ representative described the separation as mutual and stressed that both parents remained committed to raising their children together.Prescott later pushed back against what he described as “false narratives” surrounding the breakup and said his priority was being present for his daughters.The situation drew renewed attention in September after Ramos addressed pregnancy speculation online. She denied the claims and linked her improved happiness to leaving a relationship in which she alleged she had been “cheated on repeatedly.”“Hi everyone. Not pregnant!! Just very thick, eating again and happier than I’ve been in a long time!,” she commented on Instagram.“That’s usually what happens when you aren’t getting cheated on repeatedly and finally leave a situation that makes you unhappy. Hard for most of you money-obsessed people to believe, I know.”Ramos did not directly name Prescott in those comments, and the allegations have not been independently confirmed. Her current career moves, however, show a clear focus on building a future around her own ambitions while continuing to co-parent her daughters.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, has been dealing with rumors about this being his last season on the field as he eyes a Super Bowl this
articles.body: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, has been dealing with rumors about this being his last season on the field as he eyes a Super Bowl this time. While Travis Kelce focuses on the Week 5 game, he has always been public about his love and passion for Kansas City. His foundation, Eight Seven and Running, has found itself under the scanner amid money laundering claims even as he turned around the lives of two young fans through his charity.Travis Kelce gave away $100,000 to help victims of mass shooting as he focuses on winning this seasonTwo years ago, Travis Kelce’s Eighty Seven and Running, spent 100,000 on two young fans who had been brutally injured at the Kansas City Chiefs' Super Bowl LVIII victory parade when a mass shooting took place outside the Union Station.Two daughters belonging to the same family had sustained gunshot wounds and as per reports, it was Travis Kelce’s foundation, Eighty Seven and Running which gave away $50,000 to each of the girls to help them recover from their injuries.While initially reported to be 20, the number of people affected by the tragedy rose to 23 in the next following days. This includes local radio host Lisa Lopez-Galvan, who was killed in the shooting.The people who became victims of the shooting ranged between the ages of 8 and 47 years old and that half of the injured were under the age of 16.Amid the tragedy, Travis Kelce’s charity has also found itself in the news for many controversial reasons.Why is Travis Kelce’s foundation, Eight Seven and Running, in the public eye amid money laundering claims?In the last few months, public IRS filings have shown that out of $1.5 million raised, nearly $470,000 went toward high management and general expenses rather than charitable work.To make matters worse, a substantial share of management fees went to A&A Management Group. As per reports, this company has been co-founded by Travis Kelce's longtime business managers Aaron and André Eanes, with Aaron also serving as the foundation's executive director.This has raised many eyebrows among fans as the charity, Eight Seven and Running, has found itself in the public eye constantly.However, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end Travis Kelce has kept himself away from the mess and has solely focused on his season on the field.While Travis Kelce has remained closely associated with how his charity has operated, he has not spoken about it much in interviews, over the last year.Amid an unbeatable performance in the new season, many fans are expecting a Super Bowl from Travis Kelce for his seemingly last season.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ foundation gives back to children as $1.625 million commitment supports Boys & Girls Clubs
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ popular quarterback, and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, have always been dedicated in helping communities around
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ popular quarterback, and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, have always been dedicated in helping communities around them as they remain popular philanthrophics. While the popular quarterback Patrick Mahomes remains focused on the field, his foundation helped millions of children across the country.Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, gave away more than a million dollars to help childrenIn 2023, Patrick Mahomes’ foundation 15 and the Mahomies Foundation made a $1.625 million dollar contribution and a multi year commitment to support Boys & Girls Clubs of America.The 15 and the Mahomies Foundation will also gave away $1,500 for every touchdown by Patrick during the regular season in 2023.The three time Super Bowl Most Valuable Player Patrick Mahomes had opened up about it as he said, “We are truly excited to partner with Boys & Girls Clubs of America by investing in the future of children…Kids who attend a Club, like Brittany once did, are provided with the necessary tools and resources to help this generation not only thrive but lead with compassion and purpose.”The Kansas City Chiefs’ popular quarterback’s wife Brittany Mahomes added, “This meaningful partnership will expand opportunities for kids everywhere, and the places that have positively impacted Patrick and me…We are committed to doing all we can to uplift others.”In a statement, Jim Clark, president & CEO, Boys & Girls Clubs of America, said, “We are thrilled to be partnered with 15 and the Mahomies Foundation as we work to ensure all young people have the tools to reach their full potential…”Jim Clark, president & CEO, Boys & Girls Clubs of America added, “Thanks to Patrick and Brittany’s support, even more young people will have the opportunity to enjoy a meaningful Club experience. articles.title: How Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce’s $553,500 charity push gives kids more opportunities through their growing Be Philly foundation
articles.summary: Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce raised $553,500 for their Be Philly Foundation at their third annual Underdog Golf Outing on June 1, 2026.
articles.body: Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce raised $553,500 for their Be Philly Foundation at their third annual Underdog Golf Outing on June 1, 2026. The fundraiser brought 96 paying participants to Rolling Green Golf Club in Springfield, Pennsylvania. The money will support youth programs for underserved and underrepresented children across Philadelphia.The event gave the Kelces another way to support their adopted city. Be Philly, which Jason and Kylie founded in 2022, backs programs that give young people access to mentorship, academic help, career guidance and new opportunities. The foundation now has its largest group of grantees yet. Jason and Kylie Kelce put $553,500 behind philly youth programsThe June 1 fundraiser mixed charity with the kind of fun that has become familiar around Jason Kelce. Former Eagles player Brent Celek, former Flyers Scott Hartnell and Sean Couturier, and former Villanova basketball coach Jay Wright joined the golfers.Jason also brought some classic Philly energy to the course. He invited well-known Eagles fans to heckle golfers at the 10th hole. A mariachi band played near the 14th green while an Elvis impersonator moved around the course in a golf cart.The jokes had a purpose beyond entertainment. The event raised $553,500 through participant fees and sponsorships for Be Philly. Jason spoke about the foundation during the evening portion of the event. He pointed to Philadelphia's struggles with economic mobility and explained why the city remains so important to him.“Everything that I’ve had in my career and everything I’m having post-career was built because of this city and the people who have supported me and our team,” Jason told Philadelphia Magazine at the June 1 golf outing.That connection sits at the heart of Be Philly's work.Be Philly is building more opportunities for Philadelphia kidsThe foundation does not simply hand out money without a larger plan. Be Philly supports existing youth programs that already work with children in Philadelphia.In 2026, the foundation has eight grantee organizations. Their work covers areas such as youth sports, mentorship, education and support for young people facing difficult circumstances.One example is Safe-Hub's youth soccer program in Kensington. Another is Valley Youth House, which helps young people dealing with housing instability and homelessness.The foundation also supports Coded by. According to *Philadelphia Magazine*, the organization grew from serving about 350 young people each year to more than 1,200 after developing its relationship with Be Philly.That growth shows where the Kelces want their money to go. The goal is not simply to attach their names to a fundraiser. They are putting money behind programs that already work with Philadelphia children and helping those groups reach more young people.The foundation also has bigger plans ahead. Be Philly expects to distribute more than $1 million in total funds during 2026. It plans to increase its annual grant-making budget to around $500,000 by 2027. The foundation also plans to add a second grant cycle each year.For Jason and Kylie, the $553,500 raised on June 1 is another step in that plan. The golf outing lasted one day, but the money raised there can keep moving through Philadelphia youth programs long after the golfers left Rolling Green Golf Club.That gives the Kelces' latest charity effort a clear purpose. articles.title: A potential Super Bowl preview, a big NFC West showdown and hello to the byes: 5 things to know about NFL Week 5
articles.summary: We’ve got five winless teams, Mr. Irrelevant as the MVP, a Detroit Lions defense putting up historically bad numbers and a potential Super Bowl preview on Monday night. Oh, and fantasy managers, enjoy your full rosters while you can – bye weeks have officially arrived.
articles.body: We’ve got five winless teams, Mr. Irrelevant as the MVP, a Detroit Lions defense putting up historically bad numbers and a potential Super Bowl preview on Monday night. Oh, and fantasy managers, enjoy your full rosters while you can – bye weeks have officially arrived. Here are five things to know heading into Week 5. Super Bowl preview? A popular Super Bowl pick for Valentine’s Day at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, is the Buffalo Bills vs. the hometown Los Angeles Rams. On Monday night, we get a preview of exactly what that matchup could look like. The two teams arrive riding very different emotions. The Rams were down 20-10 in Philadelphia with 7:32 remaining in the fourth quarter, and the Eagles had the ball at the 2-yard line. Next Gen Stats had the Rams’ win probability at roughly 3%. Not only did the Eagles fail to score, Matthew Stafford then engineered two touchdown drives to stun Philly, 24-20. It was Stafford’s 40th fourth-quarter comeback, joining Tom Brady, Peyton Manning and Ben Roethlisberger as the only quarterbacks to reach that number. The turnaround was stunning. Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts had been 41-0 when leading by 10 points in the final five minutes of a game. That’s the kind of lead you’re simply not supposed to lose. But it also showed the veteran presence and calm this Rams team possesses. Instead of heading home with a shocking 1-3 record, Los Angeles is 2-2 and suddenly feeling pretty good about itself. The Bills are coming off the opposite experience. Their streak of 22 straight wins when leading at halftime came to an end against the New England Patriots. Drake Maye finally looked like the quarterback who finished runner-up to Stafford for MVP last season, throwing three touchdown passes, including the game-winner with less than two minutes remaining. Josh Allen, meanwhile, had his worst game of the season. Now, he faces a Rams defense that just held the Eagles to 93 passing yards – Philadelphia’s lowest total in 23 years. Oddsmakers apparently aren’t expecting another defensive struggle. The over/under for Monday night is 54.5, the highest total of the weekend. 49ers-Seahawks: NFC West showdown Nobody has gotten off to a better start this season than the San Francisco 49ers. Despite once again dealing with a mountain of injuries, Kyle Shanahan keeps finding ways to win. And if the MVP trophy were handed out after four weeks, Brock Purdy would have a pretty good case to take it home. The former Mr. Irrelevant leads the NFL with 11 touchdown passes and has thrown just one interception. Maybe even more impressive: Purdy has received elite protection. He hasn’t been sacked once through four games. The 49ers are the first team in 20 years to make it through the first month of a season without allowing a sack. That streak will be tested this weekend. San Francisco heads to Seattle to face the defending-champion Seahawks, who bounced back from a bad loss to the Washington Commanders with a win over the Chargers. Whenever the Seahawks, 49ers and Rams play one another, the stakes feel enormous. This season, that’s especially true. Every one of these NFC West matchups could go a long way toward deciding not only who wins the division, but who ultimately earns that coveted No. 1 seed in the NFC. How bad is this Lions defense? Lions fans have seen some really bad defenses over the years. This year’s version is making a run at the title of worst of the bunch. At this point, whenever Detroit is playing, just expect a shootout. The Lions are allowing 31.8 points per game. Only two teams in the last 40 years have allowed more than 32 points per game over an entire season. Those teams? The 2020 Lions and the 2008 Lions. So, yeah, Detroit has some history here. The frustrating part is that the offense has been really good. The Lions rank fourth in the NFL in points per game, and Jared Goff has thrown nine touchdown passes without an interception. Goff is the first quarterback to throw for at least 1,200 yards with zero turnovers through four games and somehow not have a winning record. The Lions visit the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, and Dan Campbell made his expectations pretty clear: “We won’t accept mediocrity on either side of the ball.” Based on what we’ve seen from this defense through four weeks, that might be easier said than done. The 0-4 Club We have FIVE 0-4 teams this season. For Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans fans, maybe that isn’t the biggest surprise in the world. But the 0-4 starts have rocked the worlds of Houston Texans, Los Angeles Chargers and Tampa Bay Buccaneers fans. And history says they should all be very worried. An 0-4 start is basically a death sentence for a team’s playoff hopes. Only one team has ever rallied from an 0-4 start to make the playoffs: the 1992 then-named San Diego Chargers, who won 11 of their final 12 games. The Texans’ start might be the most shocking of them all. Houston entered the season as a trendy Super Bowl pick. The big question was whether CJ Stroud could play well enough to support what was expected to be one of the NFL’s best defenses. Instead, the opposite has happened. Stroud has actually played pretty well. It’s the defense that keeps letting Houston down. For the third time in four games, the Texans’ defense needed just one stop to win the game – and couldn’t get it. Here’s the stat that really sums up how bizarre their start has been: The Texans are the first team in NFL history to start 0-4 without throwing a single interception over the first four weeks. The good news? We can’t have five 0-5 teams: Houston visits Tennessee on Sunday, so somebody has to win. Unless they tie, which, considering how these seasons are going, would easily be the funniest possible outcome. The bye weeks are here Bye weeks have officially arrived. Boooooooooooooooo. Fortunately, Week 5 is one of the “baby-bye” weeks, with only the Kansas City Chiefs and Carolina Panthers off. There are three baby-bye weeks this season: Weeks 5, 9 and 14. But enjoy those while you can, fantasy managers. The Bye-pocalypse is coming with six teams being off in Week 11. Consider yourself warned. articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 5 Tips, Trade Value Rankings for Top 50 Players
articles.summary: Week 4 in fantasy football threw a lot at players. Injuries, eye-popping stat lines (CeeDee Lamb had how many receptions?), Brian Robinson Jr. randomly scoring three touchdowns, etc.
articles.body:
Week 4 in fantasy football threw a lot at players. Injuries, eye-popping stat lines (CeeDee Lamb had how many receptions?), Brian Robinson Jr. randomly scoring three touchdowns, etc.

As always, how you navigate the absurdities of fantasy football comes down to the strength of the team you've built. If that team is starting to show its cracks, a timely trade could be gauze you need. And that's why we put together the weekly fantasy football trade value chart, to help you best determine whether your wheelings and dealings represent good business.

Players who would be ranked in the 51-100 range have a trade value between six and two. Players below the top-100 range have a value of one. Trade values are based on PPR scoring, so adjust according to your league's particular scoring settings. May the fantasy points be with you!

After four weeks, Lamb leads all wideouts in receptions (37) and is tied for second in targets (46). Meanwhile George Pickens has just 18 catches on 28 targets. Great news if you have Lamb, tough news if you have Pickens.

Dating back to last season, Lamb and Pickens have played together in 18 games. In the three contests last season without Lamb, Pickens caught 19 passes for 359 yards and four touchdowns. In PPR formats, that's an average of 26.3 fantasy points per game.

With Lamb in the lineup, Pickens has caught 92 passes for 1,295 yards and five touchdowns in 18 games. That's an average of 13.9 fantasy points per contest (if you look at just this season, he's averaged 10.1 fantasy points per game).

It's not a surprise that Pickens' production takes a hit with Lamb soaking up targets—look no further than Davante Adams, who was a monster without Puka Nacua this season and far more pedestrian upon his return—but you have to be realistic about the fact that Pickens is nothing more than a flex option with a healthy Lamb.

That said, he's also probably due a bit more luck in the touchdown department going forward and is still wildly talented, which means you may be able to buy super low on him at the moment and reap the benefits later. He's trending lower this season with Lamb than he did last year and that likely will normalize a bit if he starts finding the end zone.

Anybody who drafted Pickens hoping for last season's production may be incredibly annoyed at the moment. So long as you pay flex prices to land him, you can capitalize on that frustration. And if you need to throw around some of the numbers above to help push down the asking price in negotiations, well, that's what this column is all about.

articles.title: Biggest Sleepers at Every Position for Week 5 Fantasy Football 2026
articles.summary: This is the first week of team byes, so fantasy managers will need to pick up temporary replacements for Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker III, Bryce Young, Chuba Hubbard, and Tetairoa McMillan.
articles.body:
This is the first week of team byes, so fantasy managers will need to pick up temporary replacements for Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker III, Bryce Young, Chuba Hubbard, and Tetairoa McMillan.

With those fantasy stars on your bench, consider a handful of notable veterans who are slightly past their prime but have favorable or potentially high-scoring matchups. They can bail you out of a bye-week void.

Two journeyman quarterbacks headline this week's sleepers list, and a couple of tight ends over 30 are primed to be prominent targets in their teams' offenses.

Managers in point-per-reception leagues should keep tabs on a couple of running backs who may see several targets in the short passing game. Lastly, two wide receivers could take on expanded roles because of key injuries.

Here are the biggest sleepers at every position. They're all available in more than 50 percent of leagues, according to FantasyPros' consensus roster percentages.

QB Jacoby Brissett vs. Detroit Lions (22 Percent Rostered)

Brissett has made the sleeper list in consecutive weeks, and this week's home matchup against Detroit is more favorable than last week's road meeting with the Giants.

In Week 4, the journeyman quarterback threw for just 166 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions, including a pick-six.

On Sunday, Brissett will be in the comfortable confines of State Farm Stadium going against a defense that has given up the most passing yards and recorded just two interceptions this season. By the way, the Detroit Lions are allowing the most fantasy points to quarterbacks.

Lions safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph aren't ready to return from injury, so cash in on fantasy points against this defensive unit in the meantime. Brissett is primed for a top-10 finish with All-Pro tight end Trey McBride and emerging lead wideout Michael Wilson as his top targets.

QB Jameis Winston at Washington Commanders (5 Percent Rostered)

Are you ready for the Jameis Winston experience? If your league doesn't heavily penalize interceptions or pick-sixes, he is a solid replacement for Bryce Young and Patrick Mahomes, who are on bye weeks.

On short notice, Winston filled in for Jaxson Dart, who suffered a season-ending knee injury on the first drive of the New York Giants' Week 2 matchup. He played in rainy weather the following week.

In those two outings, Winston threw one interception without a touchdown pass, but last week, he provided the full fantasy experience that comes with starting him, throwing for 250 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions.

As a backup, Winston's Week 4 numbers are a typical stat line for him. Expect some big plays but bake in a couple of turnovers. He'll face the Washington Commanders, who allow the third-most fantasy points to quarterbacks and have given up 11 passing touchdowns in four games.

RB Keaton Mitchell vs. Denver Broncos (32 Percent Rostered)

Despite the Los Angeles Chargers' offensive struggles, Keaton Mitchell has seen a steady increase in touches: four, six, 11 and 15. Now handling double-digit touches and seeing a handful of targets, he's a decent flex option or a low-end RB2 for managers who need running backs.

Last week, Mitchell logged 10 carries for 39 yards, and starting running back Omarion Hampton finished with nine rush attempts for 45 yards and a touchdown. The former saw six targets, while the latter saw only two.

Quietly, the Chargers' backfield has transitioned to a near-even timeshare, though Mitchell is the more explosive tailback because of his speed. This season, he's averaging 4.6 yards per carry while Hampton is averaging four yards per carry.

The Denver Broncos allow the seventh-most fantasy points to running backs, giving up 116-plus rushing yards in three of four games. With Mitchell's expanding role, he should be on far more rosters and could be more appealing than Hampton in PPR leagues.

RB Will Shipley vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (14 Percent Rostered)

The Philadelphia Eagles may be down to their third-string running back.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo , Saquon Barkley is week-to-week with a hamstring injury, and Tank Bigsby will undergo core muscle surgery .

Will Shipley is the No. 3 running back on the depth chart, and the Eagles elevated Dameon Pierce from the practice squad. Pierce is more of a pure ball-carrier, though Shipley may see more snaps as a receiver on third down.

The Eagles selected Shipley in the fourth round of the 2024 draft. Though he's been inefficient on the ground, averaging 3.1 yards per rush attempt in 35 contests, quarterback Jalen Hurts may frequently target him in the short passing game.

Perennial All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson retired. Philadelphia traded two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens. Wideout DeVonta Smith could miss consecutive games with a hamstring injury.

Hurts may be under duress with limited options in the passing game, which would allow Shipley to take on a sizeable receiving role, and he can handle the workload.

In four collegiate years at Clemson, Shipley caught 85 passes for 602 yards and two touchdowns. He has four catches for 24 yards so far this season and should see plenty more volume against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.

WR Keon Coleman at Los Angeles Rams (18 Percent Rostered)

Last week, wide receiver DJ Moore aggravated a shoulder injury that has forced him to leave two games early this season. In those two games, Keon Coleman delivered his most productive performances of the season while taking on an expanded role.

After Moore went down in Week 2, Coleman hauled in six passes for 63 yards. In Week 4, he caught six of seven targets for 116 yards and a touchdown.

The Buffalo Bills may sit Moore to let him recover. Even if he suits up, the 29-year-old could be on a restricted snap count.

Khalil Shakir is rostered in about 57 percent of leagues. If he's not available, pick up Coleman. Both could be solid WR2s as Josh Allen's primary targets in a potential high-scoring matchup against the Los Angeles Rams. FanDuel has set the over-under total at 54.5 for that game.

WR Dohnte Meyers at Miami Dolphins (5 Percent Rostered)

Both Ja'Marr Chase (concussion protocol) and Tee Higgins (abductor) suffered injuries last week and are questionable to play Sunday. Both missed practice on Wednesday.

The Cincinnati Bengals have a Week 6 bye, so don't be surprised if the team sits its lead receivers against the winless Miami Dolphins to keep them both healthy for a midseason run.

Even if one of the two starting receivers sits out, Dohnte Meyers could take on a featured role. Last week, he hauled in seven of nine targets for 82 yards against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

The Dolphins are giving up the third-most yards per pass attempt , and the Bengals are fifth in pass attempts. Given Cincinnati's question marks at wide receiver, Meyers is worth consideration.

TE Mike Gesicki at Miami Dolphins (15 Percent Rostered)

Piggybacking off the reasons to pick up Dohnte Meyers, Mike Gesicki is also a viable target if wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and/or Tee Higgins sit out on Sunday.

Even with Chase and Higgins healthy, Gesicki has been a strong contributor to the passing game. He's caught at least three passes and scored a touchdown in three out of four contests this season.

Known for his reliable hands, Gesicki has the skill set of a big-bodied receiver. He's a 6'6", 245-pound mismatch downfield and started to show that early in his career with the Miami Dolphins between 2018 and 2022.

Gesicki is far removed from the revenge narrative in a matchup against one of his former teams, but he should be in lineups this week. The Dolphins allow the fifth-most fantasy points to tight ends and just let T.J. Hockenson rack up 13 catches for 119 yards last week.

TE Tyler Higbee vs. Buffalo Bills (3 Percent Rostered)

At 33, Tyler Higbee is back on the sleeper list because of the injuries within the Los Angeles Rams' tight end group.

After Week 3, the Rams placed second-year pro Terrance Ferguson (ankle) on injured reserve. Last week, Colby Parkinson didn't practice because of knee and shoulder injuries .

Over the last two weeks, Higbee has seen a whopping 17 targets, hauling in 13 for 129 yards and a touchdown. He knows the ins and outs of head coach Sean McVay's offense and should maintain a solid pass-catching role while Ferguson and Parkinson are on the sideline.

If Parkinson practices this week and is a full-go for Monday night, you can also consider him a sleeper option. Coming off a season in which he caught 43 passes for 408 yards and eight touchdowns, all career highs, he's rostered in just four percent of leagues.
