articles.title: Bleacher Report's Expert Week 5 2026 NFL Picks and Predictions
articles.summary: NFL Week 5 opens with a Thursday game featuring the biggest spread on the slate, followed by tighter margins on Sunday and Monday.
articles.body:
NFL Week 5 opens with a Thursday game featuring the biggest spread on the slate, followed by tighter margins on Sunday and Monday.

With a potential rebound opportunity ahead, Bleacher Report's experts broke down what could be a competitive slate.

Analysts Gary Davenport , Brad Gagnon , Kris Knox , Moe Moton , and Brent Sobleski , along with editors Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford , are coming off a week of ups and downs after a few chaotic finishes and brutal bad beats, but they're prepared for the unexpected this week.

Our lone-wolf picks are 7-5 for the season, with four more this week. Most of the panel is buying into two of the season's biggest surprise teams, backing them as road underdogs.

Moton's lead in the standings below has shrunk a bit. We'll see if the other experts continue to close the gap. Here are the breakdowns for Week 5 games.

Lines are from FanDuel as of Wednesday, Oct. 7, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Information on public betting trends is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings .

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-4) at Dallas Cowboys (2-2)

I know the Buccaneers have no business keeping it close on a short week, in Dallas, and with an undrafted rookie at quarterback. Short-week games can be weird, though, and it's already been a strange season.

Really, this isn't as much of a mismatch on paper as it might seem. Dallas' defense is still quite bad and has struggled against both the run (31st) and the pass (24th). If Jalon Daniels can avoid turnovers and make the most of his scrambling ability, the Bucs might even make this one uncomfortably close for the Cowboys.

The Cowboys have scored more than 30 points in three straight outings, including both home games. Meanwhile, the Buccaneers haven't scored more than 20 points since Week 1, with Baker Mayfield under center. Undrafted rookie Daniels will make his second start on Thursday in place of Mayfield, who has a dislocated thumb.

Daniels threw for a touchdown and two interceptions in his debut last week. New Dallas cornerback Joey Porter Jr. will likely have a full workload in this contest, and Buccaneers All-Pro defensive back Antoine Winfield Jr. will sit out with a rib injury. This feels like a matchup for the Cowboys to flex on both sides of the ball on their way to 3-2.

Cowboys: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Philadelphia Eagles (2-2) vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1)

Laying this many points for a "home" game more than 4,000 miles from EverBank Stadium gives me pause. But the Jaguars are more acclimated to playing in London than any other NFL team.

Jacksonville is playing excellent complementary football—the Jags are one bad half in Denver away from being undefeated. The Eagles likely won't have Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith or Dallas Goedert, and they're already without the now-retired Lane Johnson. That gives Jacksonville a clear edge.

I expect the Jaguars to win this game. The Eagles' roster is decimated by injuries at the moment and Johnson retired on Tuesday. The Jaguars' defense has been very good and should be able to bottle up the Philadelphia rushing attack with Barkley on the shelf.

However, this is still a veteran Eagles group coming off a tough loss to the Rams. I don't think they'll do enough to win, but Jalen Hurts comes on strong in the second half and gets the backdoor cover.

Jaguars: Davenport, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Cincinnati Bengals (2-2) at Miami Dolphins (0-4)

I was the panel's only analyst to pick Miami to cover last week in Minnesota, but that doesn't mean I'm backing the Dolphins again.

So why have I forsaken them in Week 5? They're struggling to score. Miami is averaging just 11.5 points per game and can't count on Ollie Gordon II touchdowns every week to rescue the offense. Even a beat-up Bengals team can score 20 against the Dolphins—and I expect that to be enough to cover.

The Bengals have come back to earth the last two weeks and now go on the road with both of their top two receivers dealing with injuries. Miami's defense didn't give up a touchdown in Minnesota and should keep the team in this one at home. I also don't trust Chase Brown and the Cincinnati run game to put this game away.

Bengals: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Minnesota Vikings (4-0) at New Orleans Saints (1-3)

I don't know if the Minnesota Vikings are actually any better with Kyler Murray at quarterback than they were with Carson Wentz. It certainly won't help that Justin Jefferson may miss his second full game with an ankle injury.

What concerns me about the Saints, though, is their inability to run the ball effectively and consistently (30th in rushing yards and YPC). This means a lot of pressure will be placed on second-year quarterback Tyler Shough. I'm a big fan of Shough, but I expect him to struggle against Brian Flores' defense.

Let's look past the fact that the Vikings' defense is only surrendering 12.75 points per game. I'm making this one all about the Saints.

It's not often a team should be "excited" to welcome a 4-0 opponent into its house, but New Orleans should be an exception this weekend. The undefeated Vikings, while deserving of their unbeaten mark, do not do anything particularly well offensively.

Since their 39-point outburst in Week 1, they're averaging just 15 points per game. The Saints were just pummeled on Monday Night Football for 205 yards and five touchdowns on the ground and are allowing 147.8 rushing yards and a league-worst 32 points per game; this game couldn't come at a better time. That cannot—it will not—happen again. Back-to-back home games cannot go to waste for a team trying to turn the corner of relevance.

The Saints need to capitalize on this matchup to show they can stay competitive.

Saints: Gagnon, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Las Vegas Raiders (3-1) at New England Patriots (2-2)

I don't love giving up the hook, but the Patriots appeared to figure a lot out last week and are back at home against a team they are very unlikely to overlook, given that Week 1 loss in 2025. The Raiders are a greatly improved team but are in a tough spot for a 10 a.m. body clock start.

Last week, Drake Maye had his best outing of the season, throwing for 269 yards, three touchdowns and an interception against the Buffalo Bills' 27th-ranked pass defense. He'll face a stingier Las Vegas Raiders defense that hasn't allowed more than 233 yards through the air and ranks eighth in passing yards allowed per game.

New England has turned the ball over twice in every game so far this season, and Las Vegas leads the league with nine takeaways. The Raiders' aggressive, opportunistic defense won't let this game get too far away from them on the scoreboard. They cover with a good chance to win outright.

Raiders: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Cleveland Browns (3-1) at New York Jets (1-3)

Is it time to actually believe in the Browns? It is when they're facing the Jets. With or without Mason Graham in the lineup, the Browns field a swarming and opportunistic defense.

Conversely, the Jets have struggled to finish drives and failed to move the ball last weekend against the Chicago Bears. Deshaun Watson and Co. can give the Browns enough offensively to not only cover the spread but win outright.

It's not a typo: the Cleveland Browns are 3-1. I'm actually astonished there is a favored team in this game at all. The Jets are coming off a performance in which Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai had 31 touches (30 carries, 1 reception) and the Jets offense ran 32 plays total.

Again, not a typo: Monangai had just one fewer touch than the Jets' offense ran plays all game. Other than home-field advantage, I see little reason to favor New York. Then again, Cleveland's surprising 3-1 record doesn't make the Browns an obvious choice either. Neither side inspires much confidence, but I'll give the Jets the edge at home and lay the points.

Browns: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Indianapolis Colts (2-2) at Pittsburgh Steelers (2-2)

The Colts are coming off a game in London and now have to go on the road to face a Steelers team that has had a few extra days of rest.

The Indianapolis defense ranks 31st in the league in yards allowed per game, giving Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers an opportunity to exploit a struggling unit.

I expect Pittsburgh to bounce back from its Thursday night loss, with Rodgers delivering a solid performance to secure the win.

The Colts may be on a two-game winning streak, but the rest of B/R's analysts are picking the Steelers. Logically, Pittsburgh should be favored thanks to extra prep time after a Thursday night game, and Indianapolis played in London last weekend.

However, Jonathan Taylor can take over against a Steelers defense that's middle of the pack against the run. Plus, Pittsburgh will be without defensive lineman Derrick Harmon and cornerback Jamel Dean.

Steelers: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Houston Texans (0-4) at Tennessee Titans (0-4)

The Texans and Titans are both sitting at 0-4, though it feels like Houston is closer to turning things around because we've seen it happen before—the Texans started last season 0-3 and made the playoffs.

To be fair, I do believe that Houston is the better team and its pass rush can make life miserable for second-year quarterback Cam Ward. However, I believe that the regression of Houston's defense is real and that this is a large margin for an AFC South road contest.

The Texans have won their last five games in Tennessee, but their average margin of victory is just 5.8 points, and two of the last three were decided by only a field goal.

Something has to give when two winless teams face one another. It's more likely to happen with the Texans than the Titans, especially with the way Will Anderson Jr. can heat up Tennessee quarterback Cam Ward. Last year's No. 1 overall draft pick hasn't been sacked a lot thanks to his mobility, but, outside of right tackle JC Latham, Tennessee's offensive line has not played well.

Texans: Davenport, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

New York Giants (3-1) at Washington Commanders (1-3)

Washington Commanders backup quarterback Marcus Mariota suffered an MCL injury in London last week. But according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo , starting signal-caller Jayden Daniels is "on track" to return from a dislocated elbow.

If Daniels is back on the field, this is an even matchup, and the Commanders have the hook against the spread and home-field advantage. Regardless of what Washington does, Jameis Winston will keep both teams in the game with touchdown passes and interceptions. Take the points in a go-either-way contest.

Daniels may or may not play in Week 5. It seems he's trending in the right direction, but at the time of writing, it's still up in the air.

He is 3-0 in his career against the Giants, but this is a different Giants team—not because they're shockingly 3-1 despite the absence of Jaxson Dart for all but a few quarters of the year, but because they're playing football with purpose and heart.

The Big Blue offense will rise and fall with Jameis Winston (a.k.a. The Jameis Winston Experience), but it's the defense, even without Brian Burns, that will be the deciding factor. The Giants have seen enough of Daniels, should he play, to be ready for what he brings, and New York is riding a wave of momentum it hasn't had since Brian Daboll's first season as head coach in 2022, the last time they opened a season 3-1.

A field goal with a hook on the road against a division rival is a dicey play, but these are dice worth rolling.

Commanders: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Chicago Bears (3-1) at Green Bay Packers (2-2)

Chicago Bears backup quarterback Tyson Bagent will make his second consecutive start in place of Caleb Williams, who's recovering from a hamstring injury, which may sway you toward the home-dog Green Bay Packers.

That said, the Packers have one of the league's worst run defenses, giving up the fifth-most yards and seven rushing scores.

Two weeks ago, Atlanta Falcons running backs Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. ran for 244 yards and three touchdowns against Green Bay. The Bears can do the same with the No. 1 rushing attack, featuring D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai if he's available to play with a thumb injury.

The Bears broke their curse at Lambeau Field in January 2025, snapping an eight-game road losing streak against the Packers. However, Chicago lost on its next visit in December 2025 and is 3-14 straight up against Green Bay at Lambeau since 2010.

The teams appear to be on opposite ends of the spectrum right now, health of Bears QB Caleb Williams aside, with the Bears ascending and the Packers descending, but I'm not passing up the opportunity to back a home team that historically dominates its opponent.

This is the first time since 2006 that the Packers are home 'dogs against Chicago. Even if the Bears pull out a win, I don't think it'll be by more than two points.

Denver Broncos (2-2) at Los Angeles Chargers (0-4)

The Broncos have been erratic this season, and their slow starts haven't helped. But the Chargers have struggled even more. Justin Herbert has had little protection or consistent help from his receiving corps, and the passing game has lacked rhythm.

Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's backfield rotation has left the Chargers' running game looking like a Dungeons & Dragons hydra: plenty of heads, little direction. The Chargers are a mess. Lay the points.

With all of their talent, it's hard to imagine the Chargers starting 0-5. But if they do, I think they will at least put up a fight in a desperate home game against a familiar, banged-up opponent. The hook has me on Los Angeles, along with the fact that Denver is 0-2 with a minus-31 scoring margin on the road this season.

Broncos: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

San Francisco 49ers (4-0) at Seattle Seahawks (3-1)

It's fitting that this game is being played in October, because the San Francisco 49ers are the NFL equivalent of Freddy Krueger: They just won't go away. Despite a growing injury list, the Niners keep finding ways to compete.

Landing Brock Purdy with the final pick in the 2022 draft gave San Francisco a remarkable second chance after the Trey Lance gamble failed to pay off. Now, Purdy is making his case in the MVP conversation. The Niners go to Seattle and win outright. One, two, Freddy's for you…

Eventually, the 49ers' injuries, specifically at wide receiver, will catch up to them. Playing through a rib injury, Mike Evans caught five passes for 76 yards last week, but the Denver Broncos lost starting cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss for the second half.

Seattle will be better equipped to limit Evans, Deebo Samuel Sr. and George Kittle with their No. 1 pass defense. Last year, Brock Purdy threw for two touchdowns and four interceptions in three games against the Seahawks. So his streak of stellar play could end with a loss by more than a field goal on Sunday.

49ers: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Detroit Lions (2-2) at Arizona Cardinals (1-3)

I hate picking against the Cardinals when the spread is even remotely high because Jacoby Brissett always seems to find a way to make things uncomfortable. However, in a game where I don't expect either team to be stopping much of anything, give me the team with more star power on offense to eventually pull away.

I'm expecting this game to be a shootout. Take the over as Jared Goff and the Lions get a much-needed win on the road.

Since Brissett took over as the Cardinals' QB1, Arizona has been able to do one thing very well: Throw the football, particularly late in games when the team is trailing.

Detroit's defense ranks last in the league and is the only unit allowing more than 400 total yards per game.

Brissett will sling it and rack up yards, which will likely keep Arizona close enough to cover the spread or even win.

Cardinals: Davenport, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Baltimore Ravens (3-1) at Atlanta Falcons (2-2)

It looks like we largely believe in the Falcons on Sunday, which likely stems from the fact that A) Lamar Jackson is dealing with an ankle sprain, and B) prime-time Bijan Robinson is a very real thing.

Baltimore's defense has shown tangible growth under new head coach Jesse Minter. However, I worry about its ability to hold up against Atlanta's two-headed rushing attack and the occasional over-the-top shots to Drake London. The Ravens will likely struggle to keep pace if they don't have Jackson at 100 percent.

That said, Baltimore does have a path to victory without Jackson. His name is Derrick Henry, and he could be more than enough if the Ravens force the still-inexperienced Michael Penix Jr. (14 starts) into costly mistakes.

Another prime-time game for the Runnin' Robinsons? Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. hit paydirt five times in their last outing. Going back a week before, the duo has scored eight touchdowns in the last two weeks, both nationally televised prime-time games.

The prime-time aspect probably means nothing in reality, but the Falcons have clearly figured out some things offensively, even if Penix is far from a complete or dominant QB. Jackson is questionable, at the time of writing, for the Ravens. That potential reality, plus the way Atlanta is playing right now, is more than enough to justify taking the home 'dogs here.

I'll be on the moneyline (and with both Robinsons scoring touchdowns), too.

Falcons: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Buffalo Bills (3-1) at Los Angeles Rams (2-2)

This feels like a bounce-back spot in prime time for a Bills team that has too much talent to lay another egg. The Rams have turned the ball over twice in every game they've played, and I expect Jim Leonhard's defense to capitalize on that trend with Greg Rousseau and Bradley Chubb.

This is arguably the game of the week, and it should be a high-scoring affair. The Bills suffered a predictable loss to the Patriots last week and could be without DJ Moore for this one. The Rams got a needed win over the Eagles after rallying in the second half.

I think the Rams ultimately make enough plays defensively to sneak out a win at home here, but this is a three-point game no matter who takes home the victory.

Bills: Davenport, Gagnon, O'Donnell, Sobleski

articles.title: Week 5 Fantasy Football Cheat Sheet for Best Values and Top Sleepers
articles.summary: We're only a month into the 2026 NFL season, but the fantasy landscape already looks a lot different than it did ahead of Week 1. Major injuries have impacted every single position through the first four weeks, leading managers to the waiver wire early and often.
articles.body:
We're only a month into the 2026 NFL season, but the fantasy landscape already looks a lot different than it did ahead of Week 1. Major injuries have impacted every single position through the first four weeks, leading managers to the waiver wire early and often.

Now, byes are coming into play, as the Carolina Panthers and Kansas City Chiefs will be off in Week 5. Fortunately, a few sleepers stand to provide value this week because of their projected roles or individual matchups.

Here, you'll find updated rankings for Week 5, a cheat sheet of value targets, and a look at some top options who may still be available on the waiver wire. All rankings and picks are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Sleeper: Tyler Allgeier, RB, Arizona Cardinals

Injuries have made it increasingly difficult to find viable options at running back this season. Now, Arizona Cardinals star rookie Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ailment of his own.

Love was dealing with an ankle injury heading into the regular season. After Sunday's loss to the New York Giants, head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters that Love tweaked his other ankle during the game.

This only adds to the value of Arizona's RB2, Tyler Allgeier, heading into Week 5, though he had a good amount of sleeper value anyway. Allgeier found the end zone in Week 4, yielded 12.9 fantasy points, and faces an underwhelming Detroit Lions defense in Week 5.

The Lions have surrendered the 14th-most fantasy points to opposing running backs this season. Allgeier is still available in more than half of fantasy leagues.

Stephen A. Apologizes After Lane Johnson Comments

B/R's Expert Week 5 2026 NFL Picks and Predictions

Sleeper: Tre' Harris, WR, Los Angeles Chargers

The Los Angeles Chargers are still trying to find their offensive identity under new coordinator Mike McDaniel. However, second-year receiver Tre' Harris appears to be on the cusp of being a viable flex streamer, especially in deeper leagues.

Harris has seen at least five targets in three of his four outings this season, and he's reached nine fantasy points in back-to-back games. He also faces a Week 5 matchup that isn't as daunting as it might appear at first glance.

The Denver Broncos had one of the league's top defenses a year ago, but it has largely been average this season. And while the Broncos have still surrendered the 11th-fewest fantasy points to opposing WRs, they also lost cornerbacks Pat Surtain II and Riley Moss to injuries in Week 4.

Moss may try playing through his rib injury on Sunday, but Surtain is considered week-to-week with his ankle injury, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler . Harris is available in roughly 90 percent of fantasy leagues.

articles.title: Fixing Each Winless NFL Team Ahead of Week 5
articles.summary: Entering Week 5, five winless NFL teams are looking for answers to save their 2026 campaign. Some of those clubs won't be able to right their season because of questionable coaching hires and mounting injuries.
articles.body:
Entering Week 5, five winless NFL teams are looking for answers to save their 2026 campaign. Some of those clubs won't be able to right their season because of questionable coaching hires and mounting injuries.

At this point, teams at the bottom of the standings can either make significant changes to spur a turnaround or pivot toward roster plans beyond this season.

It's a tough task, but here are bullet-point action plans to fix the winless teams: the Houston Texans, Los Angeles Chargers, Miami Dolphins, Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Tennessee Titans.

With each blueprint, we address immediate issues, though a couple also include trades that can benefit the long-term outlook of a team's roster.

Feature RB Woody Marks in short passing game

The Houston Texans need more production out of their running backs. Since David Montgomery's two-touchdown performance in the season opener, he hasn't moved the needle, averaging a career-low 2.7 yards per carry, with seven receptions for 67 yards and a touchdown.

After logging a double-digit number of touches in the Texans' first two games, Woody Marks has only touched the ball six times in each of the previous two outings. He's been inefficient on the ground since last season, which is why the Texans acquired Montgomery from the Detroit Lions, but the second-year pro should be more involved in the short passing game, where he excels as a playmaker in space.

In 2025, Marks caught 24 passes for 208 yards and three touchdowns. In three of four games this season, he has seen just one target. Houston can feature him in the short passing game as a substitute for an ineffective ground attack.

Jaylin Noel averages a league-high 23.3 yards per catch. He's shown the ability to make explosive plays primarily out of the slot, though the second-year pro can also line up out wide.

Noel has seen only eight targets in a rotational role, but after racking up a career-high 85 receiving yards last week, his snap count should be on the rise as a complement to two-time Pro Bowler Nico Collins.

Wyatt Teller lost an offseason battle for the starting left guard spot and has filled in at right guard for Ed Ingram, who missed two games with an injury. When healthy, Ingram has struggled in pass protection, allowing 10 pressures in two games, per Pro Football Focus .

Teller has made most of his 103 career starts at right guard. He could be an upgrade over Ingram and improve the Texans' 30th-ranked ground attack.

Fire OC Mike McDaniel, name Shane Day interim offensive play-caller

Yes, head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters that Mike McDaniel's job isn't in jeopardy following last week's loss to the Seattle Seahawks. Privately, he should reassess that coaching position.

Since the Los Angeles Chargers hired McDaniel, their offense has looked disjointed and hasn't shown much (if any) improvement through four weeks. Harbaugh shouldn't wait until the end of the season to re-evaluate McDaniel; he needs to dismiss him now and admit this football marriage isn't working.

Shane Day doesn't have pro play-calling experience, but he's worked with Justin Herbert as a quarterbacks coach and passing game coordinator. It would be hard for him to do a worse job than what McDaniel is doing now.

Sign the best available offensive linemen

The Chargers are dealing with a slew of injuries across their offensive line. Right tackle Joe Alt has a neck injury that could sideline him. Left guard Kayode Awosika has missed the last two outings with a leg injury.

Regardless of how the season pans out, the Chargers must protect Herbert. They should try to reunite with guard Mekhi Becton and work out the top available offensive linemen who can patch up their injury-riddled group.

At 0-4, in a tough division, with the 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders on a rapid rise, the Chargers are unlikely to climb back into the AFC West title race, especially if they lose to the Denver Broncos on Sunday.

General manager Joe Hortiz should consider trading veterans on expiring deals who may not be around beyond this season. Players such as edge-rusher Khalil Mack, cornerback Donte Jackson and inside linebacker Daiyan Henley could fetch middle-round picks in next year's draft.

Bench RT Austin Jackson for Caedan Wallace

The Miami Dolphins can improve their offensive efficiency with a few moves. First, they should make an immediate change at right tackle. According to Pro Football Focus , Austin Jackson has allowed 14 pressures and three sacks on 137 pass-blocking snaps.

Jackson's contract will expire at the end of the season. The Dolphins are unlikely to re-sign him because of his recent struggles. They should take a look at Caedan Wallace, whom they acquired from the New England Patriots this past offseason. He had a solid preseason showing at right tackle.

Acquire wide receiver talent from the trade market

The Dolphins should focus on developing their young wide receiver unit, with rookies Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr. as part of the future at the position. Still, Miami's receiver group needs another veteran who can be a go-to target.

Keep in mind that Douglas has missed the last two games because of an ankle injury. The Dolphins should inquire about young wideouts on losing teams. They can make calls on Arizona Cardinals third-year pro Marvin Harrison Jr., Los Angeles Chargers fourth-year pro Quentin Johnston, and recent Houston Texans addition Kayshon Boutte.

This is the new trend sweeping the NFL. Teams increasingly feature multiple tight ends in their offenses. Miami can follow suit by featuring Greg Dulcich in the passing game and expanding rookie third-rounder Will Kacmarek's role to bolster run-blocking schemes.

With more two-tight-end sets, Dulcich would have a better chance of playing up to the buzz he generated this past offseason, and Kacmarek could carve out a consistent role.

Fire OC Zac Robinson, tab Kevin Carberry as interim offensive play-caller

Somehow, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers watched the Atlanta Falcons' inconsistent offense under Zac Robinson for two seasons and decided to hire him as their play-caller. It's no surprise the Falcons offense is trending up while the Buccaneers struggle to move the ball.

Although Robinson has worked with quarterback Baker Mayfield in the past, his resume leaves much to be desired. Tampa Bay should relieve him of his duties and assign play-calling to Kevin Carberry.

With Carberry coordinating the run game and coaching the offensive line, the Buccaneers have rushed for 137-plus yards in two of their four games. They have a middling 17th-ranked ground attack, but it's notably better than their 28th-ranked passing offense.

Feature RB Kenneth Gainwell in the passing game

The Buccaneers must help undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels with short pass plays while he fills in for Mayfield, who has a dislocated thumb. They can do that by designing quick strikes to Kenneth Gainwell out of the backfield.

Last season, with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Gainwell excelled in a receiving role, hauling in 73 passes for 486 yards and three touchdowns.

Daniels can be a dynamic signal-caller with his mobility. In six collegiate seasons at Kansas, he racked up 1,445 yards and 23 touchdowns on the ground. In his pro debut last week, he ran for 55 yards on eight carries.

While settling into a rhythm inside the pocket, Daniels can also add another dimension to the Buccaneers' ground attack.

Feature RBs Tony Pollard, Tyjae Spears in struggling offense

The Tennessee Titans won't make a leap in the standings until they see more out of Cam Ward under center, but the best way to help him is to feature the run game. The Titans have trailed for most of the season so far, but they were competitive for a half against the New York Jets and in close games with the Philadelphia Eagles and New York Giants.

The Titans have had opportunities to feature Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears in the ground attack. Yet they rank 27th in rush attempts. On expiring contracts, Pollard and Spears will generate trade buzz, but they can be part of Tennessee's offensive identity if play-caller Brian Daboll can establish it.

Currently, the Titans are starting Atonio Mafi, whom they claimed off waivers before their season opener, at right guard. Starter Fernando Carmona is nursing an ankle injury, and his backup, Jackson Slater, is on injured reserve with a foot injury.

As a rookie fifth-rounder, Carmona had a decent showing through three games, but Becton, who played under head coach Robert Saleh with the New York Jets, can stabilize the interior of the offensive line and bolster the run game.

While it's encouraging to see rookie first-round wide receiver Carnell Tate progress in a lead role, Daboll should design more plays for the tight ends to help improve the Titans' 28th-ranked passing offense.

Gunnar Helm and Daniel Bellinger have combined for 17 targets, and both are averaging fewer than seven yards per reception. Ward can look to them as safety blankets in the passing attack.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton .

articles.title: Tom Brady said football cost him funerals and weddings, and Gisele Bündchen's second marriage gives that line a new weight
articles.summary: Tom Brady once said football cost him funerals and weddings. Four years after he and Gisele Bündchen announced their divorce on Oct.
articles.body: Tom Brady once said football cost him funerals and weddings. Four years after he and Gisele Bündchen announced their divorce on Oct. 28, 2022, that line reads differently. Bündchen married former jiu-jitsu instructor Joaquim Valente in Surfside, Florida, on Dec. 3, 2025, less than a year after Bündchen and Valente welcomed a baby boy. Brady, now a Fox commentator, has spent the same period fielding tabloid stories about his love life. The contrast between two lives that once ran together is hard to miss, and it raises a fair question about what Brady's comment really meant.Did Tom Brady say football cost him funerals and weddings?He did, though he never tied it to Bündchen. Brady made the remark on his podcast in 2022, while his marriage was coming apart in public. He was describing what two decades in the NFL had taken from his personal life. "And I can't be at funerals and I can't be at weddings," Brady said. He did not name his wife. He did not have to. Soon after, the couple confirmed the marriage was over.Context matters here. Brady was speaking about the sport's cost in general, and reading it as a message to one person goes too far. But the timing shaped how it landed. Bündchen had told Elle weeks earlier that she had concerns about his return from a February retirement, and reports had already tied the strain at home to that decision. Brady's words arrived in a house that, by many accounts, had stopped running on the same schedule. That sequence is why the funerals and weddings line was read as more than a podcast aside.How has Gisele Bündchen's life changed since the divorce?She has built a quieter, family-first life. In her split statement, she said her priority had always been Benjamin and Vivian, and that she and Brady had grown apart. Three years later she married Valente, and the family now includes a baby son.In February 2026, she joined a social media trend by sharing a 2016 time capsule. The post centered on motherhood and personal growth. Brady did not appear in it.One post proves little, and tabloids covered the omission anyway. It does show where her attention sits right now: on her children and on the home she is building with Valente, away from the NFL calendar that shaped her first marriage. One tabloid claimed she knows about the rumors linking Brady to Alix Earle and has chosen not to engage, but that report is unverified.Where does Tom Brady stand now, and does the comment still hold?Brady has built a second career away from the field, calling games for Fox. It keeps his Sundays tied to the league, only from the booth instead of the pocket. He has told PEOPLE he has little time for a personal life. Rumors have followed him anyway, from a 2023 link to Irina Shayk to chatter about Earle, an influencer, after videos from a St. Barts New Year's Eve event showed the two talking and laughing. None of it is confirmed.His line about funerals and weddings was about time, and that is the most useful way to read it today. Brady spent his time on the game. Bündchen is spending hers on a new family. As far as public reports show, Brady has never linked his old comment to her wedding, so the connection belongs to readers, not to him. Robert Irsay, father of Jim Irsay, purchased the team for $19 million. Late Jim Irsay became the owner of the Colts in 1997, when he was only 37 years old and his father had passed away.Carlie Irsay-Gordon joined the Colts as a team intern and gradually became involved in the franchise’s inner workings.She represented the team at NFL owners’ meetings as early as 2004. In 2008, she took on the role of vice president. articles.title: Drake Maye questions the moon landing, but NASA has a message ready for the Patriots quarterback’s conspiracy theory
articles.summary: Drake Maye has plenty on his plate as the New England Patriots’ quarterback, but his latest off-field comment has taken him into a very different debate.
articles.body: Drake Maye has plenty on his plate as the New England Patriots’ quarterback, but his latest off-field comment has taken him into a very different debate. During a Monday appearance on WEEI, Maye said he remains skeptical that humans landed on the moon. He did not claim to know the landing was fake, but said he was not “200%” sure it happened and described himself as “a little bit skeptical.” That was enough to draw a response from NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, who replied to a post about Maye’s comments with a short message: “I quite literally have the receipts.”Drake Maye explains why he doubts the moon landingMaye’s comments were less a firm conspiracy claim than an admission that he has not fully bought into the official account. The Patriots quarterback said he could understand why someone might have staged the landing, then stopped short of taking a clear position.“I don’t know about the moon, you know,” he said. “I think I can see back in the day why we would put on the mask if we went there, but I’m not really sure 200% if we went there or not. I wouldn’t say I’m leaning one way or the other. I just know I’m a little bit skeptical.”Maye did not present evidence that the Apollo missions were fabricated. He was talking about doubt, not offering a case against NASA.He also explained where some of his curiosity about conspiracy theories came from. While attending the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Maye said he took a course that examined conspiracy theories.“They studied [Adolf] Hitler being alive and, ‘Are birds real?’ — some of the classic ones that you hear about,” he explained.His remarks quickly moved beyond a casual radio discussion once NASA entered the conversation.NASA administrator Jared Isaacman has a simple answerNASA did not release a long rebuttal. Isaacman, the agency’s administrator, responded directly to a Boston 25 News post about Maye’s comments.“I quite literally have the receipts,” Isaacman wrote.The reply is brief, but the point is clear. NASA has a large historical record tied to the Apollo program, including mission data, photographs, recordings and physical evidence connected to the lunar missions. Isaacman chose to make that evidence the answer rather than engage Maye in a back-and-forth.The timing also gives the story an unusual NFL angle. Maye is coming off a win over Buffalo, but New England has been uneven this season and entered the week at 2-2. The Patriots are scheduled to face the 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.For Maye, the moon debate is hardly the issue that will define his season. But it has produced an exchange that is difficult to ignore: an NFL quarterback openly admitting doubt, followed by the head of NASA essentially saying the evidence is sitting there waiting to be seen.Maye’s next task is football. articles.title: NFL urges Supreme Court to let states regulate prediction markets
articles.summary: The league filed an amicus brief backing New Jersey regulators against Kalshi, arguing prediction contracts are sports bets, not federal financial instrument...
articles.body:
The NFL filed an amicus brief urging the Supreme Court to affirm that states have the authority to regulate sports prediction market contracts as gambling, joining an ongoing legal fight between New Jersey regulators and prediction market platform Kalshi.

According to CNBC, the brief contends that sports prediction contracts amount to gambling rather than financial swaps that Congress assigned exclusively to federal oversight through the CFTC — a characterization Kalshi has long disputed in its own court filings. "It is well established, however, that regulating gambling is among states' sovereign police powers," the brief states. "What constitutional power allows Congress to override states' traditional police powers to regulate intrastate gambling?"

The league cited the scale of prediction market activity tied to football, saying the sport accounted for $1.8 billion in trading on the first Sunday of the season — more than half of total platform volume that day, according to CNBC. The NFL said it is not opposed to prediction markets in principle but believes state regulators are better positioned than the CFTC to oversee them given the agency's resource constraints.

The NFL flagged a set of contract categories it views as particularly open to exploitation — among them wagers on field goals, fumbles, injuries, and officiating calls, all situations in which someone with privileged access to team information could turn an unfair advantage into profit. The league has pushed prediction platforms to eliminate those contract types entirely and to align their minimum user age with the 21-year threshold that most state sports-betting frameworks require. On Kalshi, users can be as young as 18. "Neither the CFTC nor the prediction market companies themselves — despite our persistent urging — have banned categories of bets susceptible to manipulation or set a 21 age limit," the NFL said in a statement to CNBC.

The case arrives at the Supreme Court as federal appeals courts have issued conflicting rulings on the central legal question. The Ninth Circuit ruled in August that states can enforce gambling laws against sports prediction market platforms , finding that Kalshi's sports event contracts constitute sports betting rather than federally regulated swaps. That decision created a direct conflict with a Third Circuit ruling that sided with prediction market platforms in blocking New Jersey's attempt to apply state gaming laws against them — the kind of circuit split that draws Supreme Court scrutiny.

The NFL has kept prediction platforms off its airwaves and has declined to enter into any commercial partnerships with them. Commissioner Roger Goodell said in September that the league is prepared to wait for stronger protections. "We don't feel like we have to be the first in this. We feel like we're going to be right, and the best thing to do is be patient," Goodell told CNBC. Rival leagues have moved in a different direction: the NHL has aligned with both Kalshi and Polymarket, while MLB, Major League Soccer, and UFC have each struck deals with Polymarket.

articles.title: Jason Kelce reveals what Jalen Hurts is really like inside the Philadelphia Eagles locker room
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts has been heavily criticised for the Philadelphia Eagles’ shaky start to the 2026 season. He and new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion have not p...
articles.body:
Jalen Hurts has been heavily criticised for the Philadelphia Eagles' shaky start to the 2026 season. He and new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion have not produced the results that Eagles fans were expecting.

Hurts had an excellent performance against the Washington Commanders in Week 1, throwing three touchdowns with no interceptions and posting a 122.2 quarterback rating. However, the 28-year-old has thrown four touchdowns and three interceptions over the last three weeks and has not recorded a passer rating above 86 during that span.

After beating the Commanders and the 0-4 Tennessee Titans, while losing to the Chicago Bears and Los Angeles Rams, the Eagles are 2-2 through four weeks. With the Jacksonville Jaguars up next in London, the pressure is on Hurts to raise his level and carry his team.

Jason Kelce reveals what Jalen Hurts is like inside the Eagles locker room

Jalen Hurts is one of the most divisive players in the NFL because, although he is a Super Bowl champion who consistently delivers in big moments, he often flatters to deceive throughout the regular season. He had just 93 passing yards against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4.

Many have criticised Hurts for not stepping up during a difficult period for the Eagles . As the franchise quarterback, he is ultimately responsible for leading the offense and giving his team a chance to win.

Former teammate Jason Kelce has now shared some insight into what Hurts is really like behind the scenes, especially when things are not going well. He admitted to having "tremendous respect" for the quarterback and praised how he remains neutral when the outside noise becomes louder and more critical.

"Jalen Hurts does a great job of not giving a c— what anybody says; he's one of the best at it," Kelce told The Pat McAfee Show . "I don't know what his strategy is as far as dealing with it, but coming into the building, that guy just wants to get better each and every day; he works his tail off. I have a tremendous amount of respect for how Jalen goes about trying to be the best football player he can be.

"As far as how Jalen is in the building, behind the scenes, he's one of the most dedicated people to his craft that I've been around. His temperament is [even keel]… he doesn't let stuff get to him. That guy is as cool as the underside of the pillow: he doesn't get rattled over anything."

articles.title: Nolan Wells Case: Three Young Men Sue Terrell Owens For Defamation Over Post
articles.summary: Three young men who were on the Horn Island trip where Nolan Wells disappeared are suing Terrell Owens for defamation after the NFL Hall of Famer publicly ac...
articles.body:
Three young men who were on the Horn Island trip where Nolan Wells disappeared are suing Terrell Owens for defamation after the NFL Hall of Famer publicly accused them of being involved in Wells' death.

Why did the three young men file a lawsuit against Owens?

Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo and Morgan Seymour are named as plaintiffs in a federal lawsuit filed Monday. Their fathers filed the complaint on their behalf because the three young men are considered minors under Mississippi law, according to The Associated Press and The Guardian .

The lawsuit stems from a Sept. 26 post Owens made on X, in which he wrote, "ARREST THEM IMMEDIATELY!!" He also shared a video from Instagram that alleged the three young men killed Wells and tampered with his phone, per AP.

As Blavity reported, Owens had previously pledged $25,000 toward a reward for information leading to an arrest and conviction in Wells' death.

The lawsuit alleges Owens' post contributed to death threats, harassment and public scrutiny directed at the plaintiffs. Their attorney, Edward Paltzik, said Owens' post could have harmed his clients.

"Not only is he defaming them, he's basically saying to the mob, get your pitchforks, get your torches," he said, according to AP.

The lawsuit also alleges the plaintiffs faced ridicule and ostracism, including being refused service at some public establishments, The Guardian reported.

Wells disappeared after traveling with a group to Mississippi's Horn Island during a July 4 celebration. About 30 people traveled to the island by boat. Wells remained behind while the group returned to the mainland, according to members of the group. His body was found two days later.

A Mississippi grand jury declined to move forward with criminal charges in September, saying Wells' death was consistent with drowning. His family and attorneys have continued to question the circumstances surrounding his death, including pointing to unexplained bruising and findings from the autopsy.

Attorneys for the three young men have also indicated they intend to pursue claims involving Rev. Al Sharpton and The View co-host Sunny Hostin, according to the AP and Blavity.

articles.title: Brock Purdy tops Patrick Mahomes in ESPN’s MVP rankings with rare Peyton Manning feat
articles.summary: Brock Purdy’s early MVP case goes beyond winning games. One remarkable part of his start puts the 49ers quarterback alongside Peyton Manning.
articles.body:
Brock Purdy has given the San Francisco 49ers something even more valuable than a few spectacular throws through the opening month of the season: almost no wasted possessions. That combination of big plays and remarkably few mistakes has pushed him to the top of ESPN analyst Bill Barnwell's quarter-season MVP rankings, ahead of Trevor Lawrence, Dak Prescott and Patrick Mahomes.

In his assessment of the NFL's leading award candidates through Week 4 , Barnwell placed Purdy first while making a clear distinction: These are his choices based on performance so far, rather than predictions of who will collect the trophies after the season.

For Purdy, the argument starts with a striking observation.

"Through four games, there's Purdy and then there's everybody else," Barnwell wrote.

Purdy's clean start brings a Peyton Manning comparison

According to Barnwell, Purdy became the first quarterback since Manning in 2004 to attempt at least 50 passes through the first quarter of a season without taking a sack.

That is a meaningful achievement because sacks can erase the value of an otherwise productive passing series. Purdy has also avoided fumbling and has not thrown another interception since his lone pick in San Francisco's season-opening victory over the Rams . He is doing considerably more than protecting the football, however.

Barnwell reported t hat Purdy leads the NFL with an 89.7 Total QBR, the fifth-best mark through four weeks since 2007. Three quarterbacks with higher starts in that span, Tom Brady in 2007, Manning in 2013 and Aaron Rodgers in 2020, went on to win MVP.

That history gives Purdy's opening month some impressive company, even with most of the season still ahead.

Why Barnwell gives Purdy the edge over Mahomes

Barnwell placed Lawrence second and Prescott third, with Mahomes just outside the top three in fourth.

Purdy's efficiency helps explain the separation. He is averaging 9.2 yards per dropback, according to ESPN's analysis, with Lamar Jackson the only quarterback within a yard of that figure. Barnwell also credited Purdy with producing successful plays on nearly 61% of his dropbacks, the strongest four-week start by that measure in the NFL Next Gen Stats era.

Kyle Shanahan's offense and San Francisco's talented playmakers deserve credit. Still, Barnwell noted that Purdy has maintained that production amid changing availability at receiver and a running game ranked 16th in expected points added per designed rush.

Four games cannot settle an MVP race. They can establish the standard everyone else has to chase.

Through the opening month, Barnwell's choice is Purdy.

articles.title: Chiefs Proposed Trade Pairs Patrick Mahomes With $15 Million Pro Bowl WR
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are strong candidates to trade for a wide receiver. The post Chiefs Proposed Trade Pairs Patrick Mahomes With $15 Million Pro Bowl WR...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs may have lost Tyquan Thornton for the season, while Rashee Rice is dealing with a hamstring injury that could cost him some time following the team's bye in Week 5. Those two developments have left the AFC's only undefeated squad as a strong candidate to buy ahead of the NFL trade deadline on November 10.

Multiple reports have connected Kansas City to a reunion with Tyreek Hill whenever he is healthy enough to play, which may not be until November. However, Dan Graziano of ESPN believes the Chiefs need considerably more help than Hill can provide as a replacement for Thornton, even if Rice returns healthy sooner than later.

"Stop me if you've heard this before, but the Chiefs could use another wide receiver. I'm not buying that Tyreek Hill is much of an upgrade over what they have at this point in his career," Graziano wrote on Wednesday, October 7. "If players such as Marvin Harrison Jr., Brian Thomas Jr., Jerry Jeudy or Calvin Ridley become available, the Chiefs should poke around."

Chiefs Should Consider Longevity if Team Trades for Wide Receiver in Coming Weeks

Veterans like Jeudy and Ridley make some sense for Kansas City because, as Graziano noted, the wide receiver room was already thin before the injury issues currently impacting it.

The Chiefs are resetting around quarterback Patrick Mahomes as he transitions into the second half of what is already a Hall of Fame career coming off of the worst injury of his professional tenure — a torn ACL last December.

Adding running back Kenneth Walker III looks like the move of the offseason through four weeks, as he leads the league in rushing yards and has opened up the pass game for Mahomes in ways that did not exist over the past couple of years when defenses didn't have to respect the explosive potential of the Chiefs' run game.

So while the acquisition of any reasonable pass-catcher is a needed upgrade in K.C., going after a younger player with higher longterm upside makes the most sense for head coach Andy Reid and his offense. Harrison certainly qualifies, though it Thomas who has actually proven himself in a big way at the NFL level — at least for one year.

Brian Thomas Jr. Can Offer Chiefs Buy-Low Swing on WR

The Jacksonville Jaguars selected Thomas out of LSU with the No. 23 overall pick in the first round of the 2024 draft. He is currently in the third season of his four-year, $15 million rookie contract that includes a team option for a fifth season in 2028.

Thomas hauled in 87 receptions for 1,282 yards and 10 TDs on his way to the Pro Bowl during his rookie campaign. However, he fell off inexplicably the following year, producing a little more than half of the catch totals and yardage while finding the end zone only twice.

The 24-year-old wideout has just nine grabs for 105 yards and one score through four games played in 2026, which includes only two starts. He has fallen down the depth chart in Jacksonville and profiles as a trade candidate over the coming weeks.

His value is disputable, but the Chiefs can probably buy low if Thomas becomes available. And given his cost over the next year and a half, with an option to hold onto him for another season after that, Thomas makes sense as a swing for Kansas City.

articles.title: Eli Manning Makes Head Turning Arch Manning to Jets Comments
articles.summary: 2-time Super Bowl champion Eli Manning made some head turning comments about Arch Manning potentially joining the New York Jets. The post Eli Manning Makes H...
articles.body:
Longtime former New York Giants quarterback Eli Manning was asked on the "Pardon My Take" podcast where he would prefer Arch Manning lands if he were to enter the 2027 NFL Draft.

"There's two ways I look at this," Manning said via Grace McCarron of the New York Post. "For purely selfish reasons, I wouldn't mind if he went to the [New York] Jets, just because I live right there, I could go to games, I could have dinner with him during the week a little bit. I think it'd be great for him to have some family nearby, so I wouldn't mind him going to the Jets, being up in New York…that's just my selfish reasons and I think he could help them."

This is a shocking turn of events. Eli was infamously set to be a member of the then San Diego Chargers as the No. 1 overall pick. The problem was Manning didn't want to play in San Diego, so he and the Manning family were able to force his way out. He ended up getting traded in a dramatic draft-day blockbuster to the Giants.

Most people have assumed on social media that if the Jets were ever in a position to select Arch, his family would step in and prevent that from happening. Based on these recent comments, that might be the wrong assumption.

We're still many months away from the 2027 NFL draft. We're in the middle of the 2026 regular season. However, before the 2026 college football season, the potential storyline of Arch refusing to play for the Jets got shut down.

Longtime sports columnist Gary Myers said on February 26, "I heard again this week that Arch Manning absolutely will not try to manipulate the draft (like Uncle Eli did in 2004) to avoid playing for @nyjets if they're in position to get him with [the] overall #1 pick in 2027. So relax, Jets Nation."

Eli's most recent comments seem to confirm that. If the family didn't want Arch to end up with the Jets, I strongly doubt they would be entertaining the idea on a popular podcast.

Arch Expected to Follow in Family's Footsteps

Peyton Manning was a No. 1 overall pick. Eli Manning was a No. 1 overall pick [that was eventually traded]. Arch is expected to be another Manning who becomes a high pick in the draft.

In Nick Baumgardner of The Athletic's most recent mock draft, he projected that Arch would be the No. 12 overall pick to the Cleveland Browns in the first round.

In this mock scenario, Manning was the third QB off the board. The Jets took Notre Dame passer CJ Carr with the No. 5 overall pick. With three 2027 first-round picks, if the Jets want Manning, they should have every opportunity to potentially select him or to be able to trade up to land him.

Let's just make this clear: the Jets are absolutely taking a quarterback in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft. That isn't even up for debate. The only question is who that player will be. Obviously, that piece of the puzzle is still very much up in the air, but it sounds like Manning is on the table as one of those choices.

articles.title: Boston Celtics Could Be in Mix for 20 PPG Standout With Intriguing Upside
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics could be in the mix for Vanderbilt standout Tyler Tanner, a 20 PPG guard with intriguing upside in the 2027 NBA Draft. The post Boston Cel...
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics could once again find themselves exploring intriguing prospects toward the end of the first round in the 2027 NBA Draft.

Boston has become familiar with that territory in recent years, selecting Baylor Scheierman with the No. 30 pick in 2024, Hugo Gonzalez at No. 28 in 2025, and Chris Cenac Jr. at No. 27 in 2026.

With early projections suggesting another late first-round selection could be on the cards, the Celtics may have several promising prospects to consider.

No Ceilings NBA previously projected Boston to select at No. 28, a position that could put the franchise in contention for one of college basketball's most productive guards.

Boston Celtics Could Target Standout SEC Guard in 2027 NBA Draft

No Ceilings has now ranked Vanderbilt guard Tyler Tanner as the No. 28 prospect on its initial 2027 NBA Draft Big Board, potentially placing him within Boston's projected range.

The 20-year-old is preparing to enter his junior season at Vanderbilt after establishing himself as one of the SEC's standout performers during the 2025-26 campaign.

Across 36 appearances, Tanner averaged an impressive 19.5 points, 3.6 rebounds, 5.1 assists, and 2.4 steals per game, shooting 48.5% from the field, 36.8% from three-point range, and 85.3% from the free-throw line.

His outstanding production earned him First Team All-SEC and SEC All-Defensive Team honors, while also strengthening his credentials as a potential NBA prospect.

Tanner played a pivotal role in Vanderbilt's run to the SEC Tournament Final, although the Commodores ultimately fell 86-75 to Arkansas. The talented guard contributed 15 points, five rebounds, and two steals in the defeat.

Vanderbilt also reached the second round of the NCAA Tournament before suffering a narrow 74-72 loss to Nebraska.

Despite the disappointment, Tanner delivered another impressive individual performance, finishing with 27 points and four steals.

That followed an equally productive first-round outing against McNeese, where he recorded 26 points, seven rebounds, and five assists to help Vanderbilt advance.

His ability to influence games at both ends of the floor has helped establish him as an intriguing prospect heading into another important collegiate season.

Tanner Faces Crucial Season as NBA Draft Stock Remains Uncertain

Despite his impressive sophomore campaign, Tanner's position within the 2027 NBA Draft class remains difficult to determine.

The 6-foot guard initially declared for the 2026 NBA Draft before withdrawing his name from consideration and electing to return to Vanderbilt for another season.

While his production and defensive impact have attracted attention, questions surrounding his size could ultimately influence how NBA teams evaluate his long-term potential.

"Tanner is a hard player to place within the 2027 draft," Sports Illustrated's Derek Parker recently wrote. "There's little he can truly do to massively improve his stock outside of general improvement, and he's one of the best impactors of the game in the country."

"Despite that, his size simply won't lend itself to being drafted in the upper ranks of the 2027 class. Given that class's reported weakness, he could be a safe option in the mid-to-late first round."

Those concerns help explain why early projections have offered differing assessments of Tanner's draft outlook.

The Vanderbilt standout did not feature among ESPN analyst Jeremy Woo 's initial prospects to watch, while Bleacher Report's Jonathan Wasserman previously ranked him No. 31 in the 2027 class.

Wasserman's assessment would place Tanner just outside the first round, although the difference between that ranking and No Ceilings' projection remains relatively small.

For the Boston Celtics, that uncertainty makes Tanner an interesting name to monitor. His combination of scoring, playmaking, and defensive activity could appeal to teams searching for backcourt talent, particularly if he maintains his impressive production against SEC competition.

However, with an entire collegiate season still ahead, there is plenty of time for Tanner to either strengthen his first-round credentials or slip further down draft boards.

articles.title: NFL Week 5 Storylines: Can Browns Match Best Start Since 1999 Return?
articles.summary: Cleveland eyes its second 4-1 start this century, and which 0-4 teams can get a win this week? Plus primetime NFL previews and 2-2 teams that should panic.
articles.body:
In a season with multiple surprising starts, both good and bad, the Cleveland Browns' 3-1 record is potentially the most startling.

Along with trading franchise cornerstone Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in the offseason, Cleveland also failed to make a major quarterback addition and went into 2026 with Deshaun Watson as the starter.

Expectations were low. Sportsbooks had their over/under win total set at just 5.5 .

And yet, the team is now on the precipice of something it's only accomplished one other time since returning to the NFL in 1999.

The Browns' return to the league (after the original franchise was moved to Baltimore) is not a picture of success.

Cleveland has made the playoffs just three times over the last 27 seasons and infamously, their current stadium – due to be replaced with a new one in 2029 – has never hosted a playoff game .

One of those playoff seasons, however, was in 2020 when the Browns started 4-1 and went on to an 11-5 record. It's the only time the team has started 4-1 this century, and is Cleveland's second best start since 1994, only behind a 6-1 jump out of the gates when the team was led by Bill Belichick.

There's no telling whether or not this year's Browns will be playoff-bound yet, but 4-1 is at least something that could happen again. Cleveland travels to face the 1-3 New York Jets on Sunday, and even a win there may not clarify much about this team just yet.

Both the Browns' offense and defense respectively sit in the bottom half of the NFL so far by total yardage, and the team is middle-of-the-road in terms of forcing turnovers (four so far). But Cleveland has been able to keep up a considerable pass rush, currently ranking fifth in the league with 12 sacks. Notably, the Jets have been one of the worst teams in the league at preventing sacks so far, allowing 12.

Should the Browns get past the Jets, it'll be the Baltimore Ravens up next, with the top of the AFC North potentially on the line.

A record-tying five teams are 0-4 so far, but at least one should leave that club in week five, barring a tie.

The winless Houston Texans visit the also winless Tennessee Titans in a game that effectively ends the season of whoever loses – if hope isn't lost already. But for the Texans, who had designs on the playoffs and possibly more in 2026, the bigger concern apart from the losses has been the performance of its "vaunted" defense.

Houston is allowing 260 passing yards per game (just four teams allow more) and are not forcing many turnovers. A saving grace is that they're still getting after opposing passers – the Texans have 14 sacks already. But that's also a testament to how much teams are able to drop back and throw against them. Lucky for Houston, the Titans are one of the league's worst passing teams so far.

The NFL's other 0-4 squads may not experience the same fortune, though.

Thursday night kicks off with the winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers and undrafted backup Jalon Daniels up against the high-powered Dallas Cowboys. A winless Miami Dolphins team hosts the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, and the 0-4 Los Angeles Chargers play the Denver Broncos.

About a third of the league (11 teams) is off to a 2-2 start. And while .500 is far from an emergency through four games, some of those teams are in better shape than others.

The Philadelphia Eagles are reeling after two straight losses, and are losing key players in bunches, too – with Saquon Barkley and Devonta Smith both potentially out for week five . To make matters worse for Philly, they're off to London this week to face the 3-1 Jacksonville Jaguars. A loss doesn't doom them, but with the wheels seemingly coming off on offense (the team has been shut out in the second half in each of the last two games as well), the Eagles could be in real trouble.

For the Green Bay Packers, the 3-1 Chicago Bears come to town at perhaps the worst time. Green Bay just barely survived against the Bucs , despite Tampa playing without Baker Mayfield, and the Packers look out of sorts on both sides of the ball. The Bears have had no trouble scoring without Caleb Williams these past two weeks, and they kick off a difficult stretch for Green Bay against most of the NFL's top offenses (Chicago, Dallas, Detroit, then Carolina).

Speaking of the NFC North, the Detroit Lions are in their own tough spot at 2-2. The Lions are one of three teams allowing 30 points per game so far, and let up 30 more yards per game than the next-worst group. A trip to visit the Arizona Cardinals shouldn't be cause for concern, but Arizona's been a relatively tough out this season and Detroit can't make stops.

The Atlanta Falcons have been a completely different team since Michael Penix returned from injury, and at 2-2, they now have a chance to compete atop the NFC South. To that end, they'll face a Ravens team on Sunday night likely playing without Lamar Jackson and partly as a result, played down to the lowly Titans.

Even if the game isn't competitive, it could yield some fireworks. Atlanta's scored a combined 80 points in the last two weeks since Penix came back under center.

And on Monday night, it's potentially one of the better primetime games of the year. The 2-2 Rams face the 3-1 Buffalo Bills in a rematch from 2024's 44-42 shootout at SoFi Stadium.

Los Angeles effectively rescued their season with last week's comeback against the Eagles, while the Bills lost to the rival New England Patriots and could cede control of the AFC East (for now) with a loss.

On paper, the Rams have a bit more at stake here, just because a loss drops the team to 2-3. Yet, L.A. has also played a harrowing schedule so far, with a trip to Australia, two road games (including one on the East Coast) and now a fourth primetime contest.

But for the Bills, the struggles of the last two weeks, against the Patriots and Chargers, have revealed some cracks. If the Rams exploit Buffalo's tendencies for mistakes like those two teams just did, the Bills could be in for a rough night.

articles.title: Texans Will Anderson has "a ton of respect" for Titans QB Cam Ward
articles.summary: Houston Texans All-Pro defensive end Will Anderson said he has "a ton of respect" for Titans quarterback Cam Ward ahead of their Week 5 matchup.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward is not a household name. He had a lot of success in college, particularly with the Miami Hurricanes, but that did not translate to the NFL in his rookie season and his numbers so far this season are not the greatest.

Their offensive scheme relies more on the run game with running back Tony Pollard. Pollard had a slow start to the season but seemed better in Week 4 despite the Titans losing.

Even though the Houston Texans and Titans are 0-4 going into their game against each other on Sunday, Texans All-Pro defensive end Will Anderson knows Ward is a talented quarterback and has a lot of respect for him as well as Tennessee's rushing attack with Pollard.

"He's grown a lot from his first year to now. We have a ton of respect for him," Anderson said. "He can throw the ball down the field, can escape the pocket, make plays with his legs. I think he's taking that step in his game and getting better. I know they're relying on the run game with Pollard. He's a really great running back, really good at jump cuts, can get downhill really fast. We've played a lot of games against him and we have a lot of respect for him. It's going to be a great challenge for us, but we have to stay disciplined, own your box, stay in your gaps, knock back, set edges, close when you need to close and fit everything the right way."

Ward finished 0-2 last season for the Texans, threw only one touchdown, had an interception and was sacked five times. However, Houston's defense is not playing on the same level as last season which could make them vulnerable against this young offense.

The Texans are looking to avoid starting the season 0-5 for the first time since 2005. That season, they finished the year with just two wins and claimed the No. 1 overall pick for the 2006 NFL Draft.

Current Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh was a defensive intern for Houston during 2005 and a confidant of DeMeco Ryans during their tenure on staff in San Francisco.

articles.title: The story behind Odell Beckham Jr.’s surprising Minnesota Vikings jersey number
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr. has revealed why he chose No.
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr. has revealed why he chose No. 9 after joining the Minnesota Vikings, joking that Justin Jefferson is the reason behind his new jersey number.

Beckham joined Minnesota's practice squad on Wednesday after his short return to the New York Giants ended with his release on September 29.

The Vikings moved to 4-0 with a 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, although Jefferson missed the game with an ankle sprain. Beckham now gives Minnesota another experienced option as they deal with uncertainty at wide receiver.

Odell Beckham Jr. has a long history with Justin Jefferson

No. 9 was previously worn by J.J. McCarthy before the quarterback was traded to the Giants on September 28. Beckham was therefore able to take the number, but his explanation for choosing it had much more to do with Jefferson.

"The reason I picked 9 is because Justin got half his game from me," Beckham told reporters.

There is genuine history behind the joke. Both receivers attended LSU, while Jefferson's older brother Jordan was Beckham's quarterback for one season during his time with the Tigers.

Jefferson also broke Beckham's record for receiving yards through a player's first two NFL seasons, finishing with 2,851 yards compared with Beckham's 2,755.

Beckham has made it clear that he has plenty of respect for his fellow receiver, too.

"It's amazing what he's done. It'll be amazing to get to see him up close and personal," Beckham said. "And also get to see what he's going to do for the rest of his career, god willing. He's got a chance to be the best to ever do it. It's pretty special to be able to be here with him."

He added: "Just being able to see him since coming in those days at LSU, his big brother was my quarterback, so it's a lot of history there. He's been like family to me for a long time."

Beckham's immediate role remains unclear, with Minnesota ranking last in the NFL in passing and the veteran currently on the practice squad.

Jefferson returned to limited practice on Wednesday, giving the Vikings some hope ahead of Sunday's trip to New Orleans. Beckham could now make his Minnesota debut alongside a player he has known for years, adding another chapter to their LSU connection.

articles.title: Todd McShay Drops New 2027 NFL Draft Flash Mock and Landing Spots for Arch Manning, More
articles.summary: The Ringer's Todd McShay is speculating Texas quarterback Arch Manning could end up as C.J. Stroud's successor on the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
The Ringer's Todd McShay is speculating Texas quarterback Arch Manning could end up as C.J. Stroud's successor on the Houston Texans.

Manning went to the Texans with the No. 1 pick of the 2027 NFL draft on a flash mock conducted by McShay and co-host Steve Muench on Thursday's episode of The McShay Show.

Here's a look at the results of the flash mock, which started around the 16:00 mark of the podcast.

Speculation the Texans could be planning to target a quarterback in the upcoming draft follows the team's 0-4 start to the season and their decision to let Stroud enter the 2026 campaign without an extension.

The Texans will need to decide by the 2027 draft whether the team is committing to Stroud on a long-term basis or setting themselves up to pivot toward another starter by the time his contract expires in 2028.

Whether or not Manning hears his name called at the top of the draft, McShay and Muench speculated star Ohio State wideout Jeremiah Smith is going no later than No. 2. In this mock, he would end up in Tennessee to provide help for Cam Ward ahead of his third NFL season.

Smith was ranked as the No. 1 overall prospect on the latest B/R 2027 NFL Draft Big Board .

Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore, the No. 2 prospect on the B/R Big Board, was projected by McShay to help shore up the Los Angeles Chargers' secondary at No. 4.

Miami's Darian Mensah was the only quarterback ranked as a top-10 prospect on the B/R Big Board, but he wasn't one of the four signal callers listed on McShay's flash mock.

McShay predicted Notre Dame's CJ Carr, Oregon's Dante Moore and Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss would be next off the board to the New York Jets, Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals, respectively.

At least one of the five winless clubs at the top of McShay's mock draft are on track to earn a first victory of the season this weekend. The Texans and Tennessee Titans are set to match up in a battle of 0-4 teams Sunday afternoon in Nashville.

articles.title: How Aaron Rodgers’ $3 million flag football charity push revealed the veteran’s plans beyond the NFL
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers has always had a close connection with football. In March 2024, he used that connection for something bigger than an NFL game.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers has always had a close connection with football. In March 2024, he used that connection for something bigger than an NFL game. Rodgers helped bring several current and former quarterbacks together for the third annual RX3 charity flag football tournament in Southern California. The event raised $3 million for charity. Just weeks later, Rodgers also opened up about why he sees a future for flag football beyond the NFL.Aaron Rodgers helped turn a flag football tournament into a $3 million fundraiserThe third annual RX3 charity flag football tournament took place in March 2024 in Mission Viejo, California. Rodgers helped organize the event through RX3 Growth Partners, the investment firm he co-founded with Nate Raabe and Byron Roth.The tournament brought together a strong group of NFL quarterbacks. Josh Allen and Bryce Young were among the players who joined Rodgers for the event. Their presence helped draw attention to the fundraiser and brought more NFL star power to the flag football field.That support translated into a major result. Sports Business Journal reported on May 6, 2024, that the tournament raised $3 million. The event had become one of RX3's major charity efforts since its launch.The fundraising total also showed how much the event had grown. The first RX3 charity flag football tournament in March 2022 raised $400,000, with part of the proceeds going to the Boys & Girls Clubs of America.By 2024, Rodgers and RX3 had turned the tournament into a much larger event. NFL players could compete in a relaxed setting while their names helped bring more attention to the charitable causes.The event also connected two parts of Rodgers' life. He had his NFL career on one side and his work with RX3 on the other. Flag football gave him a way to bring those worlds together.Aaron Rodgers saw flag football as more than just a charity gameThe $3 million fundraiser came at an important point for flag football. The sport was preparing for its Olympic debut at the 2028 Los Angeles Games.Rodgers spoke about that growth in comments reported by Bloomberg in 2024. He said he had enjoyed watching the sport grow and pointed to the possibility of NFL players becoming part of its future.“The recent growth of flag football has been exciting to watch,” Rodgers said in a statement reported by Bloomberg on May 4, 2024.He also suggested that flag football could become part of his own career after the NFL. Rodgers said that with the sport becoming an Olympic event and NFL players potentially getting involved, it could be part of the “next chapter” of his football career.That comment gave the 2024 fundraiser another layer. Rodgers was not simply using flag football to raise money. He was also watching how the sport could create a new path for players once their NFL careers ended.The Olympic connection made that possibility more interesting. Flag football uses many of the skills associated with traditional football but does not involve the same level of physical contact. Its inclusion in the 2028 Olympics also gives the sport a global platform.Rodgers' interest did not end with the 2024 tournament. RX3 continued the charity event in later years, showing that the fundraiser had become an annual part of the organization's work. The RX3 Foundation says the tournament began in 2022 and has continued as a recurring charity event.The numbers tell the story. Rodgers helped turn a $400,000 fundraiser in 2022 into a $3 million charity event in 2024. At the same time, he was looking at flag football as a sport with a future beyond the NFL.In Rodgers' case, the tournament offered both.
