articles.title: Sean Payton Reportedly to Be 'More Heavily Involved' in Broncos Play-Calling With Davis Webb
articles.summary: Changes are coming to the Denver Broncos' offense.
articles.body:
Changes are coming to the Denver Broncos' offense.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Broncos "are taking a more collaborative play-calling approach this week with head coach Sean Payton having an increaesd role in the process."

Schefter added that offensive coordinator Davis Webb will continue to have a "significant" hand in game-planning and game-day responsibilities.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo reported Payton will be "more heavily involved" in the play-calling.

Former Broncos wide receiver Brandon Stokley first reported on the shakeup Thursday on 104.3 The Fan in Denver, and Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio later said that Payton is taking back play-calling duties from Webb.

The move comes amid a 2-2 start for the Broncos, who rank a disappointing 27th in the NFL this season in both total offense and scoring offense.

Payton had been the Broncos' offensive play-caller for his first three seasons at the helm as head coach, but he handed the reins over to Webb ahead of the 2026 campaign.

Webb, a former NFL quarterback, had been the Broncos quarterbacks coach from 2023 to 2025, in addition to being their offensive pass game coordinator last season.

Given the overall success of the team and of quarterback Bo Nix, Webb was a hot coaching commodity during the offseason, and received multiple head coaching interviews .

Webb likely could have gone elsewhere for offensive coordinator opportunities as well, but the Broncos decided to promote him to OC and give him play-calling duties in order to retain him.

Payton had always been his own offensive play-caller, dating back to his lengthy run as head coach of the New Orleans Saints, so Webb's performance was instantly placed under the microscope.

Given that Denver was the 10th-ranked team in scoring offense in 2024 and 10th-ranked team in total offense last season, now ranking 27th in both categories through the first month of the 2026 season represents a huge fall from grace.

Nix's production has taken a major hit after putting up strong numbers over his first two NFL seasons as well.

He is completing a career-low 60.0 percent of his passes for 819 yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions.

On top of that, the Broncos have had almost no running game to speak of, as JK Dobbins leads the team with 161 yards on the ground, and Denver ranks 29th in the NFL in rushing yards per game with 81.3.

The Broncos are going on the road to face the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, and it is a hugely important game for both teams.

At 0-4, the Chargers figure to be desperate, and one can only assume they will give the Broncos their best shot.

A loss to a winless team would be devastating to the Broncos, as it would drop them to 2-3 after posting a 14-3 regular-season record in 2025.

On top of that, the Kansas City Chiefs appear to be back in form with a 4-0 record, and it could be a tough ask for the Broncos to make up a 2.5-game deficit in the AFC West, especially after already losing to KC once.

All of those factors likely played a role in Payton's reported decision, as he will look to get the Broncos' offense back to what it was over the past couple of seasons.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels 'Full Go' for Commanders vs. Giants After Elbow Injury Recovery, OC Blough Says
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is not expected to have any limitations when making his Sunday return from the dislocated left elbow he suffered three weeks ago.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is not expected to have any limitations when making his Sunday return from the dislocated left elbow he suffered three weeks ago.

Daniels is "full go" ahead of the Commanders' Week 5 matchup against the visiting New York Giants, offensive coordinator David Blough told reporters on Thursday.

Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Monday he was expecting Daniels to start Sunday against the Giants.

Daniels has been sidelined for two games after suffering his elbow injury Sept. 20 during a Week 2 matchup at the Dallas Cowboys.

The quarterback played just seven games last season in part thanks to recurring issues with his left elbow, which he dislocated in Week 9 of the 2025 campaign.

The Commanders quarterback sat out three games before returning for Week 14. He took 39 more snaps before aggravating the same elbow and sitting out the rest of the season.

Commanders general manager Adam Peters said after Daniels' latest left elbow injury the team was not considering surgery or an IR stint for the quarterback.

ESPN's Adam Schefter later reported it sounds like Daniels is "probably" going to need surgery over the offseason but is delaying the procedure in order to remain available this season.

Daniels told reporters Wednesday he considers the brace he will be wearing over his left elbow to be "kind of a part of me now."

He had previously said the brace is different than the version he wore in his Week 14 return last season because it does not allow him to fully extend his left arm.

"I'm gonna embrace it. I'm gonna embrace the brace, not really worry too much about it," Daniels said Wednesday.

The Commanders are waiting for more injury updates that will determine which offensive linemen will be tasked with protecting Daniels. Sam Cosmi and Nick Allegretti were both out last week and limited in Wednesday's practice.

Quinn said earlier this week he was "hopeful" Cosmi could soon return from his concussion. Bringing back the starting right guard could take some pressure off Daniels by boosting the Commanders' run game, which has not totaled more than 100 rushing yards in a contest since Week 2.

The Commanders (1-3) and Giants (3-1) are set to kick off Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in Landover, Maryland.

articles.title: Week 5 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em, Play or Bench Tips for Fantasy Football Managers
articles.summary: Week 4 came to a close with a huge statement win by the Atlanta Falcons and a big fantasy performance from star running back Bijan Robinson. While Robinson's performance wasn't a surprise to fantasy managers, the performance of Falcons backup Brian Robinson Jr. (62 yards, 3 TDs) might have been.
articles.body:
Week 4 came to a close with a huge statement win by the Atlanta Falcons and a big fantasy performance from star running back Bijan Robinson. While Robinson's performance wasn't a surprise to fantasy managers, the performance of Falcons backup Brian Robinson Jr. (62 yards, 3 TDs) might have been.

Brian Robinson is exactly the sort of fringe fantasy starter managers may have to count on in the coming weeks as byes enter the equation. Here, you'll find start/sit recommendations for similar matchup-based options.

As a reminder, the Carolina Panthers and Kansas City Chiefs are on bye this week. All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Jared Goff isn't a weekly must-start in the same vein as Josh Allen, Lamar Jackson, or Joe Burrow. However, he's becoming one of fantasy's better second-tier QBs because of the sorry state of the Detroit Lions' defense.

Simply put, the Lions need Goff to put up points because they're never going to win a defensive battle.

Goff has topped 19 fantasy points in each of the last three weeks and faces a strong matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Arizona has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks this season.

New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough was a budding fantasy star early in the season, and he should still be a strong streaming option moving forward. However, New Orleans' lack of a reliable ground game will make it easier for opposing defenses to focus on stopping him for the time being.

Running back Travis Etienne Jr. will miss at least four games on injured reserve.

Shough was held to just 15.9 fantasy points by the Atlanta Falcons on Monday. He'll have some favorable matchups upcoming, but this week, he'll face a Minnesota Vikings defense that has surrendered fewer fantasy points to opposing QBs than any other team.

Injuries could lead to RJ Harvey being a massive fantasy producer in the coming weeks. The Denver Broncos lost receiver Pat Bryant to an ankle injury in Week 4, and they recently placed rookie running back Jonah Coleman on injured reserve.

J.K. Dobbins is still a big part of the backfield rotation, but Bryant has emerged as a reliable receiving back and one of Bo Nix's favorite check-down options. This past week, he rushed for only 25 yards, but he also caught 10 passes for 58 yards.

This week, the Broncos will face a reeling Los Angeles Chargers team that has surrendered the 11th-most fantasy points to opposing running backs.

It's becoming impossible to trust Houston Texans running back David Montgomery, who is averaging just 2.7 yards per carry behind an underwhelming offensive line.

Montgomery isn't a significant part of the Texans' passing game plan, and he hasn't reached double-digit fantasy points since Week 1. While the winless Tennessee Titans seem like a good matchup, they're really not.

The Titans have surrendered the 17th-most fantasy points to opposing backs, and that's only because opponents have regularly been protecting a lead. Tennessee's defense actually ranks a solid eighth in yards per carry allowed (3.7).

Rookie receiver Denzel Boston is quickly establishing himself as a No. 1 option for the Cleveland Browns. He's also becoming a fringe fantasy option worth starting in all but the toughest matchups.

Boston has reached double-digit fantasy points in three of his four outings so far this season.

The New York Jets are a tougher fantasy matchup than many, as they've surrendered the ninth-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers. However, that probably has a lot to do with teams attacking their 25th-ranked run defense. Cleveland has struggled to establish the run, and it should look to get Boston involved early and often.

Cooper Kupp has been a fine complementary receiver for the Seattle Seahawks, but he's far from the fantasy superstar he was early in his career with the Los Angeles Rams. He's reached double-digit fantasy points only once this season.

Despite Seattle's lack of healthy backfield options, it's impossible to trust Kupp in a matchup against the rival San Francisco 49ers.

San Francisco has surrendered the sixth-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers this season. Managers who want to target a Seahawks receiver not named Jaxson Smith-Njigba might want to consider Rashid Shaheed, who worked into the backfield rotation and scored a rushing touchdown in Week 4.

Stephen A. Apologizes After Lane Johnson Comments

Leaving the Baltimore Ravens to join John Harbaugh with the New York Giants has allowed Isaiah Likely to emerge as a true top tight end. Even with Jaxson Dart out of the lineup, he has a reasonable fantasy floor and a high ceiling.

In Jameis Winston's second start of the season last week, Likely caught seven passes for 66 yards. This week, he has a terrific matchup in a divisional battle with the Washington Commanders.

Washington has surrendered the third-most fantasy points to opposing TEs this season.

Sit: Brenton Strange, Jacksonville Jaguars

Brenton Strange was a prominent part of the Jacksonville Jaguars' game plan in Week 4, and he finished with seven catches for 95 yards. However, he remains a matchup-based play with a bad matchup in Week 5.

Strange took advantage of a Cincinnati Bengals defense that has struggled against opposing tight ends. That helped deliver his second double-digit fantasy performance of the year, but Strange has yielded fewer than seven points in his other two outings.

This week, the Jags will host the Philadelphia Eagles, who have surrendered the fourth-fewest fantasy points to opposing tight ends.

articles.title: Trevor Lawrence, Liam Coen and the Jacksonville Jaguars bringing perfect Super Bowl recipe to Tottenham, says Neil Reynolds
articles.summary: Trevor Lawrence's Jacksonville Jaguars arrive in London with a 3-1 record at the top of the AFC South as they continue their push for a Super Bowl; watch the Jaguars take on the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium live on Sky Sports NFL from 2pm on Sunday
articles.body:
Jacksonville have enjoyed and suffered many false dawns in the past. They reached the AFC Championship game in 1999 and that was followed by five seasons missing the playoffs.

They got back to the AFC title game in 2017, coming within minutes of Super Bowl 52. That followed with four straight losing seasons. They reached the divisional round of the playoffs in the 2022 season and what followed was two more missed seasons and the firing of Doug Pedersen as head coach.

But these Jags feel different. They followed up a 13-4 season last year with three out of four wins to start 2026 and they are motivated by Liam Coen, their new head coach.

Coen came on board in 2025 and immediately changed the culture and made this team believe in itself and what he has done is accelerate himself to the very top of the NFL coaching ranks, right up there.

He should be in the same conversation as a Sean McVay and Andy Reid. He won't be Kyle Shanahan yet, but he certainly is moving into that echelon I believe and that will only be helped by further successes this season and beyond. Jacksonville have a real steel about them now because of their head coach.

I've met Coen the last couple of summers, sat down, had long interviews with him. He's a really nice guy, comes across really nice but there's an edge to him. Trevor Lawrence told me during training camp this year that Coen does a great job of instilling that chip on the team's shoulder.

The Jags, by their own admission, left meat on the bone in 2025. They came up short of their expectations given how they were playing at the end of last year so they are a very competent contender as they prepare to take on the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday. Trevor Lawrence has truly arrived as an NFL star quarterback.

He makes plays when he needs to, mistakes have become less a part of his game and he can take off and run. He's still a very athletic player and the Jags should be applauded for how they win games.

At first glance they don't have a 1,000-yard receiver, they don't have a 1,000-yard running back but they can score enough points to win and they have a collection of pieces that can make plays.

Bhayshul Tuten at running back, Brenton Strange at tight end, Jakobi Myers, Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr and Josh Cameron the rookie wide receiver coming on board this year. So it's a collection of parts, they are a team and while the stats are misleading because Joe Burrow threw for more than 400 yards, last week's road win in Cincinnati was built on defense and that is a defense that has some players.

Yes they have some stars like Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, Foye Oluokun, but again it's a team and that's what this Jaguars unit is. They are a team, they're a collection of their parts, they are not star led, they are not star heavy, they have what the Patriots kind of had back in the day when they were winning.

They have a lot of strong middle-class players. Obviously Lawrence is a star but they have a lot of steely determined players who want to win and it all stems from head coach Liam Coen. Tony Boselli has taken over the football side, he was a very aggressive offensive lineman.

Myself and Tony have been friends for 15 years, he'll give me a smile when he meets me but also looks like he wants to kill me. So that's good, they've got proper football people in the right places, the right man at head coach, the right quarterback.

Tell me that isn't a recipe to make a serious run at the Super Bowl this season and in years to come.

articles.title: Joe Burrow defends Bengals’ new offense despite Jaguars loss after previously calling for more passing in frustration
articles.summary: Joe Burrow has changed his tone about the Cincinnati Bengals’ offensive plan after their 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 4.
articles.body: Joe Burrow has changed his tone about the Cincinnati Bengals’ offensive plan after their 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 4. Burrow initially said the Bengals should throw more after their poor rushing performance, but he later admitted he may have been emotional after the game. The quarterback now says the team needs better balance and believes improving the run game is important to making the offense work.Joe Burrow explains his “throw it more” comment after Bengals lossBurrow made his original comment after a frustrating game against Jacksonville. The Bengals managed only 23 rushing yards on 15 carries, while Burrow threw the ball 54 times for 428 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. The Jaguars also put pressure on him throughout the game and finished with a 22-17 win. NFL.com reported that Burrow faced 20 pressures, his highest total in a game since Week 11 of the 2024 season.When Burrow was asked about his earlier remark, he admitted that his emotions may have played a part.“I might have been a little emotional after the game,” Burrow said, via Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. “Obviously, you want to have balance as an offense, and the run game wasn’t good enough on Sunday, and I feel confident in myself that you put it in my hands and I’m going to make it work.”Burrow also took some responsibility for what went wrong against Jacksonville. He said he could have done more in certain situations and avoided putting the Bengals’ defense in difficult spots because of the turnovers.“When you get into a game like Sunday, and they’re a really good defense, really good front seven, and I felt like we were moving the ball pretty well in the pass game,” Burrow said. “I could have been better in spots to help our guys and not put our defense in bad positions with the turnovers. We’ve got to be more balanced going forward, and a big part of that is the run game.”Joe Burrow backs Bengals’ under-center offense despite rushing strugglesThe Bengals have been working on more under-center plays and play-action concepts as part of their effort to create a more balanced offense. Burrow said that plan is not going away despite the problems seen against Jacksonville.“I’m comfortable doing whatever is needed and will execute my best,” Burrow said. “We obviously have to be better at it. We’re still going to stick with it and keep getting reps invested in that. I think it’s very valuable, so we have to be able to do it. But we need to be better.”Burrow also explained why the running game matters so much to the team’s play-action plans. If defenses do not respect the run, they can focus more heavily on rushing the quarterback, which can make life harder for the offensive line.“Under center play actions are built off the run game,” Burrow said. “Teams have to respect the run first and foremost so you don’t just get jet rushers off the edge.”For Burrow, the message is now clearer. He still believes he can carry the offense when needed, but the Bengals do not want their entire attack to depend on his arm. articles.title: 2027 NFL mock draft: First version includes a huge trade that powers Arch Manning to No. 1 spot
articles.summary: I typically avoid trades in early mock drafts, but with the Jets armed with a war chest full of draft capital, they decide to move to the top and take Mannin...
articles.body:
If you're going to kick off your first mock draft of this NFL season, might as well light some fireworks with a big trade atop the board.

The draft order is going to wildly change through the season, but that doesn't mean we can't have some fun right now. Here's my rundown, with the pick order courtesy of Tankathon .

1. New York Jets (Trade with Houston Texans) — Arch Manning, QB, Texas

Yes, the Texans have the No. 1 pick if the season were to end today. A bizarre thought just a month ago, and something I think they'll work their way out of over the next few weeks. I typically avoid trades in early mock drafts, but with the Jets armed with a war chest full of draft capital, they decide to move to the top and take Manning as their quarterback of the future. While there has been a lot of movement already on my board, especially at quarterback, Manning is still the top name at QB for me right now. His size, athleticism, pocket movement, and willingness to push the ball make for an intriguing package. It hasn't all been perfect, but Manning has already faced much tougher defenses than the other top signal-callers this season (Texas' opposing defensive schedule ranks seventh, per FEI's ratings ) and his play and process this season is cleaner when you actually get to review everything on film.

2. Tennessee Titans — Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State

I'm still not ready to move on from Cam Ward (Brian Daboll is a different story). The Titans drafted Smith's teammate, Carnell Tate, in the top five last spring and spent a decent chunk of change on Wan'Dale Robinson, which is a lot of resources spent on pass catchers. But the Titans sure still need help there. Smith is one of the best receiver prospects I've ever seen, an incredible blend of size, speed, explosiveness and hand-eye coordination. He's a true field tilter who can spearhead a passing game. He's too good of a talent to pass up. While it might not exactly be the team-building to follow, the Lions took several receivers in the first round (Charles Rogers, Roy Williams, Mike Williams) before finally striking gold with Calvin Johnson. Sometimes the talent is too good to pass up.

3. Tampa Bay Buccaneers — Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame

Moore is the other prospect I consider in the elite "purple chip" tier in this draft class. And like Smith, he's one of the best prospects I've seen at his position. An ideal mix of size, length, smooth athleticism, and advanced technique and understanding for playing his position. Moore gives the Buccaneers an elite player who can be a linchpin on the backend of their defense for years.

4. Los Angeles Chargers — Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana

The Chargers have been an absolute mess this season. While the offensive line is definitely on the priority list for the Chargers this offseason, their woes are more on the interior (although their star offensive tackle pairing have been underwhelming this year, too). Becker has an elite size and speed combination along with the ball skills to actually come down with the opportunities that his athleticism creates. He would give Justin Herbert an explosive play creator (who can actually catch the football) he's needed for years, and would also synergize with Ladd McConkey's skills perfectly.

5. Miami Dolphins — Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State

While Malik Willis has actually done nice things this season for a Dolphins team that's more of an evaluation season and doesn't have a lot of aspirations for winning football games, Miami still tabs Mestemaker here as its quarterback of the future. Mestemaker hasn't played a ton of QB, but he has good size and has a real feel for playing the position. His ball placement and ability to layer throws are standout traits. Mestemaker started the season cold but has heated up since. I think things will slow down even more for him with every rep he gets.

6. Houston Texans (Trade with New York Jets) — Jordan Seaton, OT, LSU

Now armed with two first-rounders in this exercise, the Texans will stop playing musical chairs with the offensive line room. Seaton has size, length and the easy movement skills to stay on the blindside. He would allow the Texans to move Aireontae Ersery to the right side (or keep Ersery on the same side and start Seaton on the right). Either way, it would be a boost for the Texans' offense and give Houston two real bookend tackles for years to come. Now if they can only further upgrade their run game with their next pick …

7. New Orleans Saints — Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas

The Saints could go cornerback here, but decide to build up front and get a needle mover to pair with Chase Young, who has tapped back into the talent that made him the No. 2 overall draft pick and has been a standout player since joining New Orleans in 2024. Simmons is a twitchy pass rusher with bend and has improved his hand usage this year. His relentlessness in getting after the passer, now across from Young, will be a headache for QBs and offensive line coaches for years.

8. Washington Commanders — Ashton Hampton, CB, Clemson

A young pass-catcher would definitely be in the cards here, but the Commanders absolutely need a cornerback to finally help solidify the backend of their defense. Hampton has been one of the best defensive players in college football this year, with the size, foot speed, and ball skills to be a lockdown player on the outside.

9. Arizona Cardinals — Austin Simmons, QB, Missouri

Yes, the Cardinals went with Carson Beck in the third round in the last draft, but they go with one of the biggest risers so far this season to be the quarterback of the future. Simmons can spin the football. His aggression, arm talent and weekly improvement has his stock soaring. The thought of him throwing to the Cardinals' Monstar-sized pass catchers in Mike LaFleur's system has me excited. Throw in the fact that he turns only 21 next month, and it's easy to see why Simmons' arrow is pointed up as he keeps getting better each game.

10. Cincinnati Bengals — Dylan Stewart, Edge, South Carolina

Stewart is one of the most talented players in the draft, at any position. He has had a rocky start to the season with an injury and suspension for on-field incidents after South Carolina got blown out by Alabama. But the Bengals have never shied away from players or prospects with on-field or off-field incidents. Their defense has been greatly improved this season. Stewart would give the Bengals a young ace pass rusher to pair with Dexter Lawrence II and their intriguing group of edges they added this offseason in Boye Mafe and Cashius Howell, whom I consider more of a designated pass rusher type.

11. Houston Texans (Trade with New York Jets via Indianapolis Colts) — Jadan Baugh, RB, Florida

Here's the second part of the Texans' plan to rebuild their run game. Baugh has been excellent to start the season. He's got size but is an agile runner with vision and knows how to pace and tempo his runs. Baugh would provide real juice for a Texans run game that has been among the league's worst for nearly a half-decade now and finally (hopefully) take the load off C.J. Stroud.

12. New York Jets (via Dallas Cowboys) — Will Echoles, DT, Ole Miss

The Jets could go in a few directions here. Interior offensive line, cornerback, even linebacker. Instead, they go with Echoles. He's a player the Jets would be giddy about getting at No. 12. His combination of size and quicks is actually startling with how fast he can win after the snap and get into the backfield.

13. Pittsburgh Steelers — Ellis Robinson IV, CB, Georgia

I almost pulled the trigger on Trinidad Chambliss here. The Steelers instead go with their Joey Porter Jr. replacement. Robinson is a twitchy athlete with length and ball skills. He's improved a ton this year in terms of technique and eye discipline, and he is using his traits to the fullest.

14. Dallas Cowboys (via Green Bay Packers) — Chris Cole, LB, Georgia

The Cowboys have actually been solid against the run this season, and Jaishawn Barham has been a revelation. But, the rest of their defensive spine still needs a lot of work. Safety could be in play, but instead I go with the über-talented Cole to pair with Barham to create possibly the fastest and rangiest linebacker duo in the NFL.

15. Detroit Lions — Kelley Jones, CB, Mississippi State

As the late Owen Hart would say, "enough is enough and it's time for a change." The Lions desperately could use two things: A center (Minnesota's Greg Johnson came to mind) or a cornerback. They choose to improve one of the biggest holes in the NFL right now, even with three cornerbacks off the board. Jones has been a more consistent player to start this season and can fit in both zone or man schemes. His Inspector Gadget arms head up north to Detroit.

16. Philadelphia Eagles — Trevor Goosby, OT, Texas

The Eagles' offensive line, once one of the strongest and most consistent units in the NFL for essentially a decade, has quickly turned into a unit with question marks across the board after Lane Johnson's retirement and Cam Jurgens getting traded to the Ravens this week . There are a few offensive tackles I considered here, including Goosby's teammate Melvin Siani, but the Eagles go with the massive Goosby to be Johnson's replacement on the right side. It's the perfect range for him and a proper filling of need for the Eagles who are about to be one of the most interesting teams in the NFL over the next half year (and longer).

17. Atlanta Falcons — Melvin Siani, OT, Texas

With Ironman Jake Matthews another year older and the right tackle spot being currently filled by Jawaan Taylor, the Falcons bolster their offensive line for the near-term and give themselves a succession plan for Matthews. Siani has good size (6-foot-6, 317 pounds), impressive flexibility, an ability to recover, and experience playing both tackle spots. He is a bit better as a pass protector right now, but his athleticism and developing lower body strength has me intrigued with how he will continue to progress over the back-half of the season as Texas plays tough defense after tough defense.

18. Denver Broncos — Jamari Johnson, TE, Oregon

The Broncos could go in a lot of directions here. I give them another playmaker on offense in Johnson, a true three-down tight end who has excellent ball skills and the ability to stretch the field. He also has some blocking chops, even if it's not always perfect at this point in time. Johnson has great balance and YAC ability to maximize the plethora of screens and underneath throws that Bo Nix prefers.

19. Carolina Panthers — Greg Johnson, OG/C, Minnesota

There have been so many teams I wanted to pair with Johnson. He's one of those players who boosts his teammates around him as a solidifying force with his smarts and sound play. He has real athleticism and pop to his blocks, too. Johnson has positional versatility, but his best spot long-term will be at center. Either way, he gives the Panthers options to shore up their offensive line, both right away and down the road.

20. New England Patriots — Trey'Dez Green, TE, LSU

Josh McDaniels likes his tight ends. Drake Maye likes throwing to his tight ends. The Patriots have to continue to add talent to their offense, so any position makes sense here. Hunter Henry will be 32 in December and has tangibly slowed down, even if he still is a solid player. Green is a massive target who looks and plays like the former basketball player that he is. He has excellent ball skills and has developed his strength, which has shown up as a blocker and when working through contact. He's also not stiff getting in and out of breaks and with the ball in his hands. Green injured his knee and is still working his way back, but pairing him with 2026 third-round selection Eli Raridon would give the Patriots a massive tight end room with catching range and real athleticism for Maye to fire throws to for years to come.

The Browns keep firing away at the quarterback position and go with the exciting Chambliss. He is going to be a conundrum for talent evaluators throughout this process. His age (he'll be a 25-year-old rookie) and lack of ideal size (6-foot, 205 pounds) will give some pause, but his film and production might be too good to pass up. I really like Chambliss, even with his age and size outliers. His arm talent, timing and willingness to work from the pocket and fire throws all over the yard — including over the middle of the field — will translate to the next level. And he has real athleticism to throw on the run and create as a passer and runner, too. It's a fine line between "fun" and "good." I think Chambliss is both.

22. Cleveland Browns — Yhonzae Pierre, Edge, Alabama

Pierre is a relentless pass rusher who can also set the edge in the run game and drop into coverage when needed. He has developed his pass rush plan this year, and has shown more strength. I like the thought of pairing Pierre's speed across from the bull rush-heavy Jared Verse on the other side.

23. Las Vegas Raiders — Cam Coleman, WR, Texas

Coleman could go much higher than this, but what a boon for the Raiders this would be if he slipped this far. Coleman is a true X receiver who has been a bit inconsistent this year, but still oozes talent. His size (6-foot-3, 204 pounds), ball skills and twitchiness cannot be taught. The Raiders' offense has been one of the more fun ones this season, even if it's unusual as they trot out tight end and fullback-heavy looks and most of their targets are funneled to those positions. Coleman would give the Raiders a real outside threat to pair with Brock Bowers and give Fernando Mendoza one of the league's most exciting crop of young skill players for the future.

24. Seattle Seahawks — Cayden Green, OG/OT, Missouri

The Seahawks sneakily have one of the NFL's best guard and tackle duos in Charles Cross and Grey Zabel, but their right guard position has been a spot where recent coaches have just been trying to mitigate the damage, and it's been a revolving door this year with players). I'm one of the higher people on Green, who has now been a standout player at guard and tackle in his college career. He would instantly shore up the right guard spot for the Seahawks, while also providing some positional versatility if needed.

25. Jacksonville Jaguars — Tae Johnson, Safety, Notre Dame

The Jaguars' coaching staff does a great job of getting the most out of their players on both sides of the football. I thought about the trenches here, and there are some intriguing names the Jags could go with on both sides (as you'll see over the next few picks). Instead, they select the supremely talented Johnson. He has tremendous range on the backend and the playmaking ability in both the run game and as a blitzer. He would be fun for defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile to manage (if Campanile doesn't get a head coaching job this offseason, that is.)

26. Buffalo Bills — Kingston Lopa, Safety, Cal

Back-to-back safeties! The Bills outright need more defensive talent. They are currently one of the worst defenses in the league and their defensive backfield lacks playmakers. Lopa has been one of the biggest risers this season, not only because he's been productive with five interceptions, but he's a unique player with elite size and versatility at his position. He's listed at 6-foot-5 and lines up in the slot and in the box at times. He would be a huge upgrade over what the Bills have now. Lopa can impact the game and give Jim Leonhard a queen on the chessboard who can actually do something over the course of a game.

27. New York Giants — David Stone, DT, Oklahoma

The Giants are currently getting by with veterans on their defensive interior. D.J. Reader has been firmly good this season against the run and pass, but he is 32 years old. Stone has battled an injury this season and in 2025, but he's seemingly good to go and could make a big impact this week against Texas. He's stout and strong enough to hold up against double-teams, and flashes quickness and versatility to align across the defensive line.

28. Chicago Bears — Boubacar Traore, Edge, Notre Dame

Whether it's at defensive tackle or edge, the Bears need more talent up front. I go with Traore here. He's a strong, heavy-handed edge defender who compares favorably to Jared Verse. Traore can not only help set the edge against the run, but he can also give the Bears' front the pocket-pushing ability that coordinator Dennis Allen loves with his players.

29. Baltimore Ravens — Lance Heard, OT, Kentucky

Trenches were an easy pick for me with the Ravens, whether it be on offense or defense, especially with the top tight ends off the board. Heard is a joy to watch as he bulldozes defenders in the run game. He has length and enough athleticism to stay on the outside, but his strength would also translate nicely on the inside if needed. He would also provide depth if Ronnie Stanley continues to battle injuries. He reminds me a bit of former Raven Kelechi Osemele.

30. Minnesota Vikings — Kade Pieper, C, Iowa

I was VERY tempted to tab a quarterback here for the Vikings. Drake Lindsey, CJ Carr, Darian Mensah, and Nico Iamaleava were all considered, but I hesitate to push any into the first round just yet. Instead, the Vikings solidify another position they've cycled through names and that touches the ball every snap, going with Pieper to man the pivot spot for years to come. Pieper is a good athlete and a great fit for teams that want to major in zone-running schemes, like the Vikings have preferred under head coach Kevin O'Connell.

31. Kansas City Chiefs — Nick Marsh, WR, Indiana

There is a nice crop of wide receivers here for the Chiefs to choose from. While they might want a true speedster, like Ole Miss' Deuce Alexander or even Alabama's Ryan Coleman-Williams (in the midst of a bounce back season this year), they instead go with Marsh. I love Marsh's game. He has strong hands, and very good body control and balance. He's very quarterback friendly as a pass catcher and has a knack for finding soft spots against zone. And he's an excellent blocker. He's just a useful and reliable player who can play inside and outside, and the Chiefs need more players like that for Patrick Mahomes.

32. San Francisco 49ers — Zereoue Williams, OT, Utah

Every year, I tab the 49ers with an offensive tackle in these mock drafts, swearing that this is the year Trent Williams falls off and they select his long-term replacement. Trent Williams has battled an injury already, but his play has definitely not fallen off. And yet here I am again, back at it with another tackle with the same last name in Zereoue Williams. Williams is an easy-moving athlete with enough pop as a blocker to play on both sides of the football. Kyle Shanahan is the best at working with whatever offensive line talent he has. Williams would give him a player who could be useful for the short-term and give him a plan for whenever Trent Williams decides to hang them up. Which might never happen at this rate.

articles.title: Kelvin Sheppard Defends Blitzing Bryce Young Despite Lions' Struggles in Loss to Panthers
articles.summary: Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard doubled down on his decision to continually blitz Bryce Young in a Week 4 loss to the Carolina Panthers.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard doubled down on his decision to continually blitz Bryce Young in a Week 4 loss to the Carolina Panthers.

"Those calls were the right calls, and I'll leave it at that," Sheppard told reporters Thursday.

When asked about a potential disconnect between play calling and execution, Sheppard said, "Those are private conversations that we have that I'm going to keep in house. Those calls were the right calls."

Young went 7-for-8 when blitzed on 12 dropbacks during the Panthers' 32-26 win over the visiting Lions last Sunday, per 100.9 The Mitt's Ben Bosscher and Pride of Detroit's Al Karsten.

Young now leads all quarterbacks in passing yards under pressure (411) through four games, per NFL Next Gen Stats .

The Lions are now preparing for a Week 5 matchup at the Arizona Cardinals this Sunday.

Sheppard said Thursday he found it "ultra disrespectful" to be asked if the Lions felt their offense needed to carry the team amid the defense's struggles.

"I can care less about the talk. It's all poison, and I mean that. Every word of it's poison, and I told the players," Sheppard said.

The defensive coordinator also said he was "absolutely not" changing his evaluation of what his unit can accomplish heading into Week 5.

"I'm standing firm in my beliefs... We have a certain way we said we are going to play, and we are," Sheppard said.

"Now, do you tweak things here and there?... Yeah, that's football. But to just outright bring in a new playbook every week because the last one didn't go right, that, to me, leads to ultimate dysfunction and the dam completely broken."

So far this season, the Lions rank third among NFL teams in pressure rate (46.6 percent) and first in non-blitz pressure rate (48.2 percent), per The Score's Sam Hoppen .

Aidan Hutchinson and Alim McNeill have also helped the Lions rank fourth in the NFL in ESPN's pass rush win rate through Week 4.

That hasn't been enough so far to limit explosive plays from opponents. Detroit has allowed the most total yards against of any NFL team during their 2-2 start to the season.

The Cardinals are heading into this weekend's matchup on a three-game losing streak during which they surrendered at least 31 points in each contest.

Arizona's offense has still been active, scoring a combined 54 points in their last two losses at the San Francisco 49ers and New York Giants.

Sheppard, who is in his second season as the Lions' defensive coordinator since his promotion from linebackers coach in 2025, will be tasked with limiting Jacoby Brissett when the Week 5 matchup kicks off Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET in Glendale.

articles.title: NFL calls prediction markets a form of sports gambling, urges courts to let states regulate
articles.summary: The National Football League filed an amicus brief arguing prediction markets like Kalshi should face state gambling regulation over game integrity.
articles.body: The National Football League has made its stance clear on prediction markets. In an amicus brief on Thursday, the league said that the sites fall under the sports gambling umbrella and should similarly be regulated by states. "Billions of dollars will be bet on NFL games through prediction markets each season, and any delay from the Court will result in increasing consumer harm and risk to game integrity," the NFL wrote in the brief, via ESPN. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The league sent a letter to prediction market operators just before the start of the season saying they objected to markets like coaching and officiating decisions, injuries, and other markets that could be swayed by insider info. The league has yet to partner with predict markets but does have deals with official online sportsbooks. "The [Commodity Futures Trading] Commission's failure even to reference such objectionable contracts that the NFL identified months ago -- contracts that have been and continue to be listed as contracts by operators like Kalshi -- is deeply concerning and creates significant risks for the NFL's players, coaches, and officials and market participants," the league said. The CFTC, however, said that it has been in touch with the league as prediction markets have risen, but the league has not entered an agreement with them to work together. "Since day 1, the CFTC has engaged with the NFL regarding the agency’s rulemaking agenda and policy priorities. It’s unfortunate the NFL declined to sign an MOU with the CFTC which would’ve provided the league the ability to better discuss, cooperate, and exchange information with us to promote the integrity and resilience of prediction markets," Brooke Nethercott, public affairs director for the CFTC, told Fox News Digital. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER A CFTC source said that "just weeks ago, several senior NFL staff members notified senior CFTC staff that they were on the verge of commercial partnerships with several prediction market operators." Kalshi also took a shot at the NFL for not being "willing to share data and collaborate to protect game integrity." "Kalshi’s top priority is the integrity of its markets. That priority is reflected in the fact that other major sports league and integrity partner in the United States is partnering with Kalshi—including the MLB, NHL, USTA and others," Kalshi told Fox News Digital. "Contrary to the NFL’s statements, the CFTC is actively policing sports-related markets, which are now listed on nearly every US commodities exchange. The CFTC’s ongoing rulemaking addresses many of the NFL’s supposed concerns. And those rules sit atop the same comprehensive system of federal enforcement that protects trillions of dollars of transactions in US markets." A source from the CFTC also said that the NFL's brief "makes clear that it is most interested in regulating the regulator, not game integrity." "While this bullying tactic may work in the states, the CFTC will not be subject to regulatory capture, which is exactly why the federal framework established by Congress is the most effective way to regulate prediction markets," the source said. "This is not about the NFL opposing prediction markets..." an NFL source said. "If the CFTC were to adopt the same robust regulatory approach as states, this would be less of an issue... "For years, ever since sports betting on prediction markets started to gain traction, the NFL has been closely engaged in the relevant policy discussions. This is about protecting game integrity and consumers—just like legalized sports betting. There have already been billions of dollars in NFL wagers on prediction markets this season. Given this volume of trading and the uncertainty around it, it is critical for the Court to act as soon as possible. But it is unclear if the Commission has the resources or staff to adequately regulate sports betting." articles.title: Tony Romo disqualified from golf tournament the same day he parted ways with CBS after OWI arrest
articles.summary: Tony Romo ran into an issue with his scorecard on the final day of a pre-qualifier.
articles.body:
Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback and CBS television analyst Tony Romo was disqualified from the final round of a Korn Ferry pre-qualifier tournament on Oct. 2, the same day he parted ways with CBS over his July OWI arrest.

Romo, who was attempting to make the cut for the Korn Ferry Tour, was accused of signing his score card with the wrong scores on two holes , per Golf.com.

Romo reportedly signed for a 4 on 16 and a 4 on 17 on his own scorecard. Problem was, his marker, Brandon Rice, had Romo marked down for a 4 on 16 and a 5 on 17. And when another pro reviewed Romo's score, that pro believed Romo actually shot a 5 and a 5.

When contacted, Romo reportedly took responsibility for the error. Since he signed for a lower score than he should have received, Romo was automatically disqualified from the event. He did not perform well enough to make the cut on the final day of the pre-qualifier, so the disqualification didn't affect his outcome.

PGA Tour rules official Rob Keller — who spoke to Romo over the phone about the violation — said a number of factors may have resulted in the error. In addition to Romo likely being frustrated over his play, his trio was operating at too slow a pace, resulting in the players being put on a clock.

The rushed nature of their play, combined with Romo's frustration and inability to inch closer to the cutline, likely resulted in the mistake, Keller told Golf.com.

Throughout his NFL career, Romo also established himself as a talented amateur golfer. He's attempted to qualify for a number of professional events over the years and won a celebrity event in 2018.

Following his NFL career, Romo became an analyst with CBS. He initially received high marks for his abilities as a broadcaster. Romo's rise eventually resulted in him becoming the top color commentator for CBS.

But that came to a halt in July, when Romo was arrested for OWI (operating while intoxicated) after a golf event in Wisconsin.

CBS put him on leave a few days later and left his status undetermined until months later, when the network and Romo mutually agreed to split .

articles.title: NFL Urges the Supreme Court to Rule on Regulation of Prediction Markets
articles.summary: The NFL is urging the Supreme Court to rule on the regulation of prediction markets, arguing in an amicus brief filed Thursday that states — which already regulate legal sports books — are better positioned to oversee sports-related contracts "given the current landscape."
articles.body:
The NFL is urging the Supreme Court to rule on the regulation of prediction markets, arguing in an amicus brief filed Thursday that states — which already regulate legal sports books — are better positioned to oversee sports-related contracts "given the current landscape."

The NFL is supporting New Jersey's request for the Supreme Court to rule on the governing authority for prediction markets, which provide an opportunity to trade — or wager — on the result of future events. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has maintained it has exclusive federal jurisdiction, while states have argued that the array of typically yes-or-no questions is akin to gambling and falls under their purview.

"Absent the clarity that only this Court can provide, (prediction market) operators will continue exploiting the gap between state and federal regulation, endangering consumers and the integrity of sports events across the country," lawyers for the NFL wrote.

According to the NFL's brief, on the first Sunday of this season, more than half of the trading volume on prediction markets — $1.8 billion out of $3.3 billion total — was related to the league.

"Any delay from the Court will result in increasing consumer harm and risk to game integrity," the NFL wrote in its brief.

Kalshi spokeswoman Elisabeth Diana said its top priority is market integrity, and she pointed to its partnerships with the NHL, Major League Baseball and other sports organizations as evidence.

"Contrary to the NFL's statements, the CFTC is actively policing sports-related markets, which are now listed on nearly every U.S. commodities exchange," Diana said. "The CFTC's ongoing rulemaking addresses many of the NFL's supposed concerns. And those rules sit atop the same comprehensive system of federal enforcement that protects trillions of dollars of transactions in U.S. markets."

A Polymarket spokesperson said the operator "shares the NFL's commitment to preserving the integrity of the game," and it is working on "a harmonized federal framework that delivers a stronger, more consistent form of integrity compared to a patchwork of disconnected state laws built for a bygone era."

Ohio filed a brief on Wednesday urging the high court to side with New Jersey and preserve the power of all states to regulate prediction markets, as they do casino gambling and sports betting. The filing was backed by 38 states, including Republican and Democratic attorneys general from states including Arkansas, California, Illinois, Missouri, New York, South Carolina and Pennsylvania.

Roughly 20 states are involved in litigation over prediction markets , and a split has formed between appeals courts, making it more likely that the Supreme Court will take up the issue. The 6th and 9th U.S. Circuit Courts of Appeals have ruled in favor of states seeking to regulate prediction markets, while the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals agreed with Kalshi in a ruling earlier this year.

"As between the two approaches, the NFL believes the Sixth and Ninth Circuits got it right, given the current landscape," lawyers for the league wrote in their brief.

The NFL also is questioning the CFTC's enforcement capabilities. In its filing, the league writes that the commission has 543 employees and their responsibilities include a range of derivatives beyond event contracts.

"Without adequate staff engaged in oversight and enforcement, even the best regulations cannot meaningfully ensure game integrity and consumer protection," lawyers wrote in the NFL brief.

A message was left by the AP seeking comment from the CFTC.

The NFL has urged the CFTC and prediction markets to adopt a list of prohibited wagers that it feels pose the greatest threats to game integrity, according to the brief, but they have declined thus far. It also has asked the commission to adopt an age limit of 21 for trading on prediction markets, up from the current 18.

Diana said Kalshi has tried to collaborate with the NFL on market integrity, but it has received no response.

articles.title: NFL Shares Record-Breaking Special Teams Stat Through 4 Weeks of 2026 Season
articles.summary: The NFL's desire to make the special teams more exciting for fans when the dynamic kickoff was implemented has paid off.
articles.body:
The NFL's desire to make the special teams more exciting for fans when the dynamic kickoff was implemented has paid off.

Per numbers from Troy Vincent Sr., executive vice president of the NFL's football operations department, the 13,409 kickoff return yards so far this season are the most ever through the first four weeks in league history.

There have been a total of 516 returns between the 32 teams, an average of roughly 26.0 yards per return. This is right in line with the 2025 season average (25.9), but slightly down from 2024 when it was at an NFL-record 27.6 yards.

However, the 2024 season only averaged 1.7 kickoff returns per game. This season averages 4.0 returns per contest.

Dylan Laube of the Las Vegas Raiders leads the NFL in kickoff return average with 33.4 yards on seven returns. Myles Price of the Minnesota Vikings leads the league in total return yards (423) and ranks third in yards per return (30.2).

One interesting nugget is despite the overall success teams are having on kickoff returns, there has yet to be a kickoff return touchdown thus far. There were six during the 2025 season.

The NFL originally implemented the dynamic kickoff in 2024, but it really took off last season after owners voted to approve a rule change that spotted the ball at the 35-yard line on touchbacks instead of the 30-yard line.

articles.title: Derrick Henry Calls Bijan Robinson NFL's 'Best' RB, 'I Ain't Going to Shy Away From it'
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens' Derrick Henry apparently doesn't feel he's currently the NFL's best running back.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens' Derrick Henry apparently doesn't feel he's currently the NFL's best running back.

Henry called the Atlanta Falcons' Bijan Robinson "the best in the game right now" when speaking to reporters ahead of a Week 5 matchup between the Falcons and Ravens.

"He's doing it all," Henry said Thursday (h/t the Baltimore Banner 's Jonas Shaffer). "I ain't going to shy away from it. He's doing a great job."

Robinson is heading into Week 5 with 494 rushing yards, the second most in the NFL, despite a relatively slow start to his 2026 campaign.

The Falcons star was held to fewer than 85 rushing yards in each of his team's season-opening losses at the Pittsburgh Steelers and to the visiting Carolina Hurricanes.

Robinson saw his production jump after quarterback Michael Penix Jr. returned in Week 3.

He has racked up a total of 339 rushing yards and four touchdowns in consecutive road wins at the Green Bay Packers and New Orleans Saints.

Robinson and the Falcons are looking to ride that momentum into the matchup against a Ravens team dealing with uncertainty while Lamar Jackson nurses an ankle injury.

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said earlier this week he doesn't expect the team's offensive game plan to change much if the team turns to backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. The Ravens have already relied on Henry, who ranks fourth in the NFL with 374 rushing yards, to play the majority of offensive snaps so far this season.

The defense could be making more adjustments. Defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said it was a possibility the Ravens could deploy three linebackers in packages designed to limit Robinson.

Whichever quarterback is starting for the Ravens, Henry and Robinson will be expected to play key roles for their respective teams when the Week 5 matchup kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET Sunday in Atlanta.

articles.title: 49ers warned over injury to 10-time Pro Bowler amid multi-week absence
articles.summary: What will the Niners do?
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have unfortunately dealt with many injuries over the past couple of years, a big reason this team hasn't been able to win a Super Bowl.

If the 49ers had stayed healthy on both sides of the ball, we'd likely be saying very different things about this organization. Instead, that injury bug keeps popping up, and it already has this season with fullback Kyle Juszczyk.

While he won't put up major numbers, at least not in the run game as a fullback, he currently has four carries and does a lot more as a blocker and through other factors that help the 49ers' offense.

That's why an ESPN insider recently suggested that his absence could be a big problem for San Francisco.

"I might think … the Kyle Juszczyk loss for the 49ers is a game-losing injury," ESPN's Ben Solak wrote

"Juszczyk, who left Sunday's game against the Broncos in the fourth quarter, has a bone bruise and is out for three to four weeks. Normally, a fullback injury might go unnoticed — heck, any injury for a player with four touches through four games. But Juszczyk has gone in motion on 61 snaps, second only to Buccaneers WR Emeka Egbuka. Among non-ball carriers, he is more integral to the 49ers' running game — both as a point-of-attack blocker and his versatility on where he lines up — than any other skill position player in the league. The 49ers should still throw the ball well, but bringing a one-dimensional offense into a game against the Seahawks feels perilous."

It'll be interesting to see what Kyle Shanahan wants to do with Juszczyk injured, since there really isn't a perfect replacement for him right now. After being selected in the fourth round of the 2013 NFL Draft, he's built a really nice career for himself doing small things like that.

articles.title: NASA Administrator Fires Back at Patriots’ Drake Maye Over Moon Landing Comments
articles.summary: Drake Maye has spent the week being praised for his performance against the Buffalo Bills. Now, the New England Patriots quarterback has caught the attention...
articles.body:
Drake Maye has spent the week being praised for his performance against the Buffalo Bills.

Now, the New England Patriots quarterback has caught the attention of someone considerably farther removed from the NFL.

What began as an unexpected admission during Maye's weekly appearance on WEEI has turned into a viral exchange after the 24-year-old revealed he isn't entirely convinced the United States landed astronauts on the moon in 1969.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman apparently couldn't resist responding.

"I quite literally have the receipts," Isaacman wrote on X after seeing a clip of Maye's comments.

It was a pointed, five-word response to a quarterback who had just helped deliver New England's biggest win of the season.

And it wasn't exactly the kind of attention Maye was expecting to generate during a routine radio appearance.

NASA Administrator Responds to Drake Maye's Moon Landing Doubts

Maye's comments came Monday, Oct. 5, during an appearance on WEEI, one day after the Patriots defeated the Bills 29-26 in Buffalo.

The conversation took an unusual turn when the subject of the Apollo 11 moon landing came up.

"I don't know about the moon, you know," Maye said. "I think I can see back in the day why we would put on the mask if we went there, but I'm not really sure 200 percent if we went there or not."

Maye wasn't ready to commit to either side of the debate.

"I wouldn't say I'm leaning one way or the other. I just know I'm a little bit skeptical," he added.

The Patriots quarterback also offered some background on his interest in conspiracy theories, explaining that he studied the subject while attending the University of North Carolina.

"They studied [Adolf] Hitler being alive, and, 'Are birds real?' — some of the classic ones that you hear about," Maye said.

It didn't take long for those remarks to travel well beyond New England sports radio.

Boston 25 News shared a clip of Maye discussing the moon landing on X, where Isaacman responded with his comment about having the receipts.

And unlike the average person weighing in on a moon landing conspiracy theory, Isaacman happens to run the agency responsible for putting Americans on the lunar surface.

Apollo 11 landed on the moon July 20, 1969. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first two people to walk on its surface, while Michael Collins remained in lunar orbit.

The mission left behind an extensive scientific record, including photographs, lunar samples and equipment that continues to provide evidence of the Apollo program's achievements.

Maye, for his part, didn't offer any evidence that the landing was staged. He simply acknowledged having doubts about an event that occurred more than three decades before he was born.

That was apparently enough to get NASA involved.

Drake Maye's Viral Comments Follow Patriots' Biggest Win of Season

The timing of the exchange makes the story even more unusual.

Only days earlier, Maye had given Patriots fans plenty to celebrate with a performance that helped New England pull off a road victory over its AFC East rival.

The quarterback completed 22 of 37 passes for 269 yards and three touchdowns against Buffalo, overcoming two first-half turnovers to help the Patriots improve to 2-2.

His final touchdown pass was also his most memorable.

With less than two minutes remaining, Maye connected with wide receiver Efton Chism III on a spectacular one-handed touchdown catch that helped New England secure its 29-26 victory.

It was a much-needed afternoon for Maye, who had entered the matchup facing criticism over his turnover problems and New England's 1-2 start.

Even after the win, Maye wasn't pretending everything had been fixed.

"It's relieving a little bit," he said afterward. "I know I've got to play better and still left some stuff out there today. But we've got to build on it."

That remains the priority for Maye and the Patriots as they prepare to host the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 11.

Las Vegas enters the matchup at 3-1, while New England has an opportunity to climb above .500 for the first time this season.

For Mike Vrabel and the Patriots, the focus is on carrying Sunday's momentum into another important game.

For Maye, it has also been a reminder that when you're an NFL quarterback, even an offhand comment about something that happened in 1969 can become national news.

Especially when the person responding has NASA on his résumé.
